items.title: [Bug]: zero-match casing probe is hint-only — withholds the paths it already found, sends weak models into re-search spirals (measured +6 turns)
items.body:
## Summary

The zero-match casing probe from #77011 is hint-only: it reports that case-insensitive matches exist but withholds the file paths it already found. Strong models pivot in one turn; weak models spiral into repeated re-searches. Measured on the A/B eval rerun (2026-08-06, private repo `NousResearch/hermes-toolperf-evals`, `results/2026-08-06_rerun/`): `err_case_search` on qwen3-coder-30b went from 3.3 turns / 13s (baseline, no probe) to 9.3 turns / 40s (fixes) on 2 of 3 reps. Sonnet-4.5 shows no effect.

## Evidence (ATOF traces, checked into the eval repo)

The probe fires with:

```json
{"total_count": 0, "warning": "0 exact matches, but 2 case-insensitive match(es) in 2 file(s) — the pattern's casing may be wrong."}
```

qwen's response on rep 0: **5 consecutive `search_files` calls** trying casing variants, then 7 `read_file` calls — 12 tool calls for a task the baseline arm solved in ~2. Rep 2: same shape via terminal grep detours (10 calls). The probe already ran the case-insensitive search to produce that count — it knows the 2 paths and throws them away.

## Fix direction (auto-DO over hint-only)

When the case-insensitive probe finds matches, include them in the result instead of only warning:

- `case_insensitive_matches`: the actual match list (or first N paths + counts), clearly labeled as coming from an `-i` search
- Keep `total_count: 0` for the exact pattern so the semantics stay honest

Same principle as the tool-batch's other winners (recovery recipes DO the recovery): the data is already computed; handing the model a hint but not the answer taxes exactly the models the probe was built to help.

Likely same shape in the sibling probes from #77011/e7aa06c3a6 — the hidden/gitignored probe also reports counts without paths; worth fixing as a class.

## Repro

```bash
# private repo NousResearch/hermes-toolperf-evals
cd abeval && ABEVAL_HOME=<configured-home> \
  python3 ab_eval.py run --arm fixes --model qwen/qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct \
  --reps 3 --pythonpath <main-tree> --only err_case_search
```

Related: the `err_hidden_search` mixed visible+hidden gap (probe only fires on total-zero) found by the original Aug 2 run is still open on both arms — same probe family, could be fixed in the same pass.

items.title: Plugin SDK crashes with React #310 when any desktop plugin is loaded on Windows (v0.20.0 / v2026.8.3)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary
After the v0.20.0 (v2026.8.3) updater replaced the desktop binary on Windows 11, the app crashes at boot with `Minified React error #310` ("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render") whenever any user-installed desktop plugin exists in `desktop-plugins/`. Removing ALL plugin files fixes the crash immediately.

## Reproduction
1. Install Hermes desktop v0.20.0 on Windows 11
2. Place ANY plugin.js in `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/desktop-plugins/<name>/plugin.js`
3. Launch Hermes → white screen with "Something broke in the interface"
4. Remove the plugin file → app boots normally

Reproduced with: a minimal plugin registering a single component with one static `useValue` hook, zero network calls, zero conditional hooks. Any registration triggers the crash.

## Environment
- Windows 11 build 26200
- Hermes desktop v0.20.0 (commit 3c27eb623, tag v2026.8.3)
- npm 11.17.0 (for rebuilds — also tested with the updater's pre-built binary)
- Electron with React 18, bundled app.asar

## Diagnostic evidence (CDP capture)
Attached Chrome DevTools Protocol to the live crashed app. The crash originates from a JIT-compiled Blob URL (the plugin SDK's runtime JSX compiler):

```
Error: Minified React error #310
  at Object.render (blob:file:///d9153ab7-edbd-4274-99db-11a35b4e5f8b:115:35)
  at index-0ApWPtU_.js:13:49424
  at Array.map (<anonymous>)
  at Gde (index-0ApWPtU_.js:13:49119)   ← pane layout component
  at Oo (vendor-react-R-OdkZd7.js:8:47520)
  at yc (vendor-react-R-OdkZd7.js:8:69943)
```

Window globals at crash: `__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`, `__HERMES_REACT_JSX__`, `__HERMES_REACT_JSX_DEV__`

The error boundary DOES work — shows "Something broke in the interface" with Retry/Reload/Open logs buttons.

## What was ruled out (13 hypotheses, full matrix available)
- Not a corrupt database (tested with empty state.db)
- Not config corruption (tested with pre-migration config.yaml)
- Not theme (tested dark/light, native-theme.json)
- Not GPU/environment (--disable-gpu still crashes; "Gpu Cache Creation failed: -2" is a non-fatal disk-cache permission error, confirmed via Chromium source)
- Not a specific plugin's code (crashes with ANY plugin, even a single static hook)

## Root cause
The plugin SDK's component wrapper creates a hook-count mismatch when any user plugin is registered. This affects ALL user-installed plugins regardless of their code. Built-in plugins (command palette, etc.) are not affected.

## Workaround
Remove all files from `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/desktop-plugins/`. The app works normally.

## Impact
All Windows desktop users who have installed any user-created desktop plugin after the v0.20.0 update cannot launch the app.

## Related
This is separate from issue #79428 (2nd-window crash — also React #310, reported 2026-08-05). That issue covers a different trigger path. The boot crash reported here is new in the v2026.8.3 updater build and is reproducible with zero window interaction.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop remote OAuth/gated mode — inline audio/video never plays (`?token=` auth seam is loopback-only; media elements can't send Bearer/cookie)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes Desktop (macOS) is connected to a **remote gateway running in gated/OAuth mode** (`auth_required: true`, `/login` interstitial), inline `MEDIA:` audio/video attachments render as a black player stuck at 0:00 and never play; the player then falls back to an "Open video file" / "Open audio file" button. Downloading the same file through that button works fine (authenticated bridge fetch), and the file plays natively — so the bytes and path policy are fine. Only inline playback is broken.

This is the **gated-mode variant of closed #72207 / #44748**. PR #73521 (v2026.7.30) fixed remote playback for loopback/token-auth gateways, but the fix's auth mechanism cannot work against a gated gateway, so the bug persists there.

## Root Cause

**Desktop side** — `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`, `mediaExternalUrl()` (called by `resolveMediaPlaybackSrc()` for remote audio/video):

```ts
if (isRemoteGateway()) {
  const conn = $connection.get()
  if (conn?.baseUrl && conn.token) {
    return `${conn.baseUrl}/api/files/download?path=${file}&token=${encodeURIComponent(conn.token)}`
  }
}
```

The `<video>`/`<audio>` element's only credential is the `?token=` query param.

**Server side** — three independent reasons that URL can never authenticate against a gated gateway:

1. `hermes_cli/web_server.py` `auth_middleware` (~line 658): when `app.state.auth_required` is true, the legacy `_SESSION_TOKEN` / `_has_valid_query_token` check is **skipped entirely** ("The legacy _SESSION_TOKEN path is loopback-only"). `_QUERY_TOKEN_API_PATHS = {"/api/files/download"}` is dead code in gated mode.
2. `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py::gated_auth_middleware` accepts only (a) `Authorization: Bearer <provider access token>` verified via the provider stack, or (b) session cookies. A `<video>`/`<audio>` media-element fetch can set **neither** — no custom headers, and the RFC 8252 native-app flow deliberately sets no cookies ("goal: no session cookies", token rotation via `/auth/native/refresh`).
3. `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/token_auth.py` (token-auth seam) reads only the `Authorization` header, and `/api/files/download` is not a registered token route anyway.

Additionally, even where the query seam is active (loopback mode), it compares against `_SESSION_TOKEN` (`HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` env or random per-boot) — a value the desktop's OAuth `conn.token` is **not** (it's the provider-minted access token).

**Why downloads still work**: "Open video file" → `downloadGatewayMediaFile()` → `readDesktopFileDataUrl()` → `bridge().api()` — the Electron main process attaches `Authorization: Bearer` to those calls. The media element is the only unauthenticated path.

## Live Evidence (against a gated gateway, auth_required: true)

```
$ curl ".../api/files/download?path=..."                       # no credential
401 {"error":"unauthenticated","reason":"no_cookie","login_url":"/login"}

$ curl ".../api/files/download?path=...&token=<bogus>"          # what the <video> element sends
401 {"error":"unauthenticated","reason":"no_cookie","login_url":"/login"}   # ← identical: ?token= never consulted

$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <bogus>" ".../api/files/download?path=..."
401 {"error":"session_expired","reason":"invalid_or_expired_session"}       # ← bearer path exists and is evaluated
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Hermes gateway with dashboard auth enabled (OAuth gate; Docker install behind `https://host:9119` with `/login`).
2. Connect Hermes Desktop (macOS) in remote mode via OAuth login.
3. Have the agent produce any `MEDIA:/path/clip.mp4` (or `.mp3`) attachment in chat.
4. Observe: black player, 0:00, no metadata; then "Open video file" fallback appears.
5. Click it / download — file arrives intact and plays in a native player.

## Environment

- Desktop: macOS Hermes Desktop v0.20.0 (remote mode, OAuth)
- Gateway: Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (Docker, `auth_required: true`), Starlette 1.3.1 (`FileResponse` does support Range — not the issue)
- Reproduces on any video/audio format; images unaffected (they use the bridge data-URL path)

## Suggested Fix Directions

**A. Server: verify `?token=` as a bearer candidate for `/api/files/download` in gated mode.**
In `gated_auth_middleware`, for this one route, when neither bearer header nor cookies are present, run the query token through the same `_verify_bearer` provider stack instead of returning `no_cookie`. Minimal change; mirrors the `_QUERY_TOKEN_API_PATHS` precedent; makes the already-shipping desktop URL work. Caveat: provider access token appears in URLs (access logs, browser history).

**B. Server + desktop: short-lived signed media tokens (preferred long-term).**
Renderer calls an authenticated bridge endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/files/media-token {path}`) → server returns an HMAC-signed, path-scoped, short-TTL token → renderer appends `?mt=...` → download route verifies signature only. No bearer in URLs, no server-side state, no cookie needed.

**C. Desktop-only fallback (rejected before, see PR #70076)**: fetch bytes via the bridge into a blob: URL. Loses HTTP Range/seeking and hits the 100 MB data-URL cap — the reason the streaming path exists.

## Related

- #72207 (closed) / #44748 (closed) — same symptom, loopback/token-mode ancestors, fixed by #73521
- #76936 (open) — sibling `MediaAttachment` dead-end for `kind === 'file'` in remote mode
- #61457 (open) — desktop session-cookie persistence against gated gateways
- PR #63808 (open) — native save bridge for remote files

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram gateway goes permanently deaf after network outage — reconnect watcher never fires (fatal handler wedges)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

After a ~30-minute ISP outage, the Telegram gateway becomes **permanently deaf** even after the network recovers: the process stays alive (`systemctl` sees it as `active`), but no reconnect happens, no messages are received, and the only recovery is a manual `systemctl --user restart`. This happened on **2026-08-06** with all 16 gateway instances, requiring manual restart of all of them.

This is the same symptom class as #3173 ("gateway becomes unresponsive ~25 minutes after transient network error"), which was supposedly fixed by #3268, and #70344 ("reconnect watcher wedge after network-loss fatal error"), which is **already merged into the code we are running** — yet the failure still reproduced. So the existing fixes do not cover this path.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent HEAD: `87ca9613e5` (2026-07-30) — includes #70344 fix (commit `83fe362e80`)
- python-telegram-bot: 22.6
- OS: Ubuntu (Linux 6.17.0-35-generic), Lenovo Legion Y540
- Setup: 16 gateway instances (root + 15 profiles), all under `systemd --user`, `Restart=always`

## Timeline (2026-08-06, all times EDT)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 15:53 | ISP outage begins — `api.telegram.org` unreachable |
| 15:55 | Telegram polling times out, enters retry loop (`attempt 4/10` → `10/10`, 60s max delay) |
| 16:04:04 | 10 retries exhausted → adapter logs `Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway.` and sets fatal error `telegram_network_error` (retryable=True) |
| 16:04:04 | `gateway.run` logs `Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error)` — **this is the LAST `gateway.run` log line for 21 minutes** |
| 16:04 → 16:25 | **No** `queued for background reconnection`, **no** `Reconnecting telegram (attempt N)`, **no** `staying alive` log. Process alive (MCP logs continue), cron scheduler still fires, but Telegram never reconnects |
| 16:25 | Manual `systemctl --user restart` of all 16 gateways → recovery |

## Key Evidence: the fatal handler never reaches the reconnect queue

`_handle_adapter_fatal_error` (gateway/run.py:4290) logs the fatal error at line ~4314, then is supposed to:

1. queue the platform via `self._failed_platforms[...] = ...` + log `queued for background reconnection` (line ~4359)
2. if no platforms remain and none queued → `Shutting down gateway for service restart` (line ~4369)
3. if no platforms remain but queued → `gateway staying alive, watcher will retry` (line ~4384)

**None of lines 2/3 ever appear in the journal.** The last `gateway.run` line is the fatal-error log itself. Combined with the process staying alive (MCP logs continue, cron continues), this indicates the fatal-error handler is **stuck inside its own execution** — most plausibly in the `await self._safe_adapter_disconnect(adapter, adapter.platform)` path (line ~4347) when the adapter's `disconnect()` blocks on a half-dead socket, or in an await that the 5s `_adapter_disconnect_timeout_secs` wrapper does not actually bound (e.g. an inner `asyncio.gather` on lifecycle tasks that catches `CancelledError`).

Because the handler never returns, `_failed_platforms` is never populated, so `_platform_reconnect_watcher` has nothing to reconnect — **even after the network comes back**. The 5s disconnect timeout also did not produce its own `Timed out after 5.0s while disconnecting` warning, which suggests the hang is not (only) in `_safe_adapter_disconnect` itself but in an await it waits on that swallows cancellation.

## Log excerpts

```
15:55:21 WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Telegram network error (attempt 4/10), reconnecting in 40s. Error: Timed out
16:02:44 WARNING ...: [Telegram] Telegram network error (attempt 10/10), reconnecting in 60s. Error: Timed out
16:04:04 ERROR hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway. Last error: Timed out
16:04:04 ERROR gateway.run: Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error): Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway.
16:04:48 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '3e144bf9739f': delivery error: Telegram send failed: Timed out   <- gateway alive, telegram dead
16:08:12 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: ... will self-probe every 300s ...                        <- process alive, event loop alive
# (no gateway.run logs between 16:04:04 and 16:25 manual restart)
```

## Expected Behavior

After a retryable fatal telegram error, one of these must happen automatically:

1. **Best**: the adapter is queued for background reconnection, the watcher reconnects it once the network returns, **without restarting the gateway process** (in-process state, cron, sessions preserved). This is the documented intent of the current design but does not happen because the handler wedges.
2. **Fallback**: if the handler cannot complete (e.g. `disconnect()` on a half-dead transport), the gateway must eventually exit so systemd `Restart=always` recovers it — bounded by a hard timeout that cannot be swallowed by inner awaits.

Either way: **after the network recovers, the gateway must come back without manual intervention.**

## Suspected Root Cause

The fatal-error handling path is not fully bounded. `_safe_adapter_disconnect` has a 5s timeout wrapper, but:

- the wrapper's `_await_adapter_cleanup_with_timeout` releases the *runner* at the deadline but detaches the inner task (`consume_detached_task_result`) — the caller can proceed only if the awaited path actually returns
- `adapter.disconnect()` contains multiple inner awaits (cancelling lifecycle tasks via `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)`, `updater.stop()` with its own `_UPDATER_STOP_TIMEOUT`, `app.stop()/shutdown()`, status indicator, pending delivery cancellation) — if any of these swallows `CancelledError` while blocked on a half-dead socket, the fatal handler never returns, the queue is never populated, and the watcher never reconnects.

The #70344 fix hardened `_connect_adapter_with_timeout` (the *connect* path) and added `_ensure_reconnect_watcher_running()`, but the fatal-handler *disconnect* path appears to still be able to wedge. Suggest auditing all awaits in `_handle_adapter_fatal_error` / `TelegramAdapter.disconnect()` for cancellation-swallowing hangs, and/or adding an outer hard deadline so the fatal handler always returns and the reconnect queue is always populated.

## Impact

- Gateway becomes permanently unresponsive after network recovery (~30 min outage in this case, would be indefinite without manual intervention)
- No automatic recovery; requires manual SSH + `systemctl --user restart` on each affected gateway
- All 16 instances affected in this report
- Related: #3173 (same symptom, closed by #3268), #2910 (silent delivery failure), #70344 (watcher wedge, partial fix)

## Local Workaround (for users hitting this)

A cron watchdog that checks `gateway_state.json` platform state + the `state/gateway.heartbeat` file, and restarts only the affected gateway when the network is up but telegram is not connected for >5 minutes (strike-twice before acting). Happy to share the script or discuss upstreaming a bounded-recovery design.

## Summary

A reference-only context-compaction handoff can become the active user turn after an already completed assistant response and cause Hermes to resume stale historical work. This reproduces the stale-task class that #41607 / #42812 reported as fixed by #44454.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)`
- Commit: `a88b76bf7`
- Platform: Linux Desktop app
- Source: long Desktop tool-calling session
- The checkout contains the #44454 historical-framing fix.

## Observed sequence

The affected session accumulated five compaction messages totalling 164,110 characters. The decisive sequence was:

1. An assistant response completed normally and was persisted with `finish_reason = stop`.
2. Hermes inserted a 32,052-character message with role `user` beginning `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]`.
3. No new human request appeared after that handoff.
4. The compaction message was marked active and contained a historical task snapshot describing work that had already been completed.
5. Hermes immediately began a new tool-calling turn and resumed that stale historical task.

The handoff itself explicitly said not to answer or fulfil requests from the summary. Nonetheless, because it was the only active user-role message after the completed response, it functioned as a fresh actionable turn.

## Expected behavior

- Internal compaction must not create a new actionable human turn after an assistant response has already completed.
- A reference-only handoff must never by itself trigger model continuation.
- If compaction occurs while preserving a pending real user message, that message must remain separately identifiable and must be the sole active instruction.
- Historical task snapshots must remain data, regardless of topical overlap.

## Actual behavior

The compaction handoff became the active user message and stale work resumed without a new human request.

## Regression context

- #41607 — `Compression summary stale instructions executed as current task`
- #42812 — `Stale compaction Active Task hijacks resumed sessions after idle timeout`
- #44454 — merged fix that removed the topic-consistency carveout and reframed summary headings

This incident occurred after those changes were present, and has a stricter shape: there was no post-summary user message for the model to privilege. The synthetic reference summary itself occupied the active user slot.

## Relation to #80449

#80449 describes oversized single turns defeating the compaction token budget. That may explain the repeated 15k–46k-character summaries seen here, but it does not explain why a completed turn was followed by model execution driven solely by a synthetic reference handoff. The stale-task execution should therefore remain a separate regression.

## Suggested regression tests

1. Persist a completed assistant `stop` response, trigger compaction, and assert that the synthetic summary does not initiate another agent turn.
2. Trigger compaction while a real user message is pending; assert that the real user message remains outside the summary and drives the next response.
3. Include a historical snapshot containing an apparently executable task and verify that no tool calls occur without a later real user message.
4. Assert that compacted synthetic `role=user` records cannot be mistaken for user-originated turns by the gateway/session dispatcher.

No private task text, project names, filesystem paths, or session identifiers have been included.

items.title: no_agent script cron jobs disappear from jobs.json while gateway is running (CLI-created jobs clobbered by scheduler state)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

`no_agent` (script-only) cron jobs **disappear from `jobs.json` while the gateway is running**. Jobs created through the `cronjob` tool are never persisted; jobs created via the `hermes cron create` CLI persist for a while and are then **overwritten/removed by the gateway's in-process scheduler state**. Agent-based cron jobs are unaffected.

This makes the documented watchdog pattern (`--no-agent` + script, empty stdout = silent) unreliable on a running gateway: the alert job silently vanishes and never fires.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)
- Profile-based install (`HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/<name>`), gateway running as `hermes gateway run`
- In-process cron scheduler (`cron.scheduler_provider`: "In-process cron scheduler started (interval=60s)")
- All jobs were `no_agent=true` with a script under the profile's `scripts/` dir, schedule `every 2m`, `repeat=0` (forever)

## Observed incidents (all with a live gateway, no gateway restart in between)

### Incident 1 — job created via the `cronjob` tool, vanished during a CLI `cron remove` of another job
- `2026-08-04 20:17:24.455` — `jobs.json` rewritten as `{"jobs": [], ...}` while the watchdog job was still listed moments earlier. Job never ran afterwards.

### Incident 2 — job created via the `cronjob` tool, never persisted at all
- `2026-08-07 00:11:28.336` — `cronjob(action="create")` returned success with a full job object (`id=6fe656430928`, `no_agent`, script, `every 2m`), but `jobs.json` was written empty at the exact creation timestamp. `hermes cron list` → "No scheduled jobs" immediately. No execution was ever recorded in `executions.db`.

### Incident 3 — job created via CLI, persisted, then clobbered by the gateway ~30 min later
- `2026-08-07 01:00` — `hermes cron create "every 2m" ... --no-agent --script check_session_220928.sh --repeat 0` → success, and `jobs.json` **did contain** the job (`jobs: ['5cbe7b847aac']`), verified right after creation; `hermes cron list` showed it `[active]`, next run `01:10:32`.
- `2026-08-07 01:31:06.146` — `jobs.json` rewritten empty (`{"jobs": [], "updated_at": "2026-08-07T01:31:06"}`), ~30 minutes after creation, **before** the first scheduled run. The gateway ticker heartbeat confirms the scheduler was alive and ticking (60s interval). The job never fired, and `hermes cron remove 5cbe7b847aac` then reported "not found".

For comparison, an **agent-based** job (`no_agent=false`, prompt only) created via the `cronjob` tool on the same gateway persisted and ran correctly every 5 minutes for 10+ hours.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the gateway: `hermes gateway run` (in-process scheduler).
2. Create a watchdog job via the CLI while the gateway is running:
   ```bash
   hermes -p <profile> cron create "every 2m" "watchdog" \
     --name "watchdog" --no-agent --script check.sh --repeat 0 --deliver origin
   ```
   (or via the `cronjob` tool with `no_agent=true` + `script`).
3. Immediately verify: `cat $HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json` → job present (CLI path) or already empty (tool path).
4. Wait ~30 minutes (no gateway restart): `cat $HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json` → `{"jobs": [], ...}` — job gone, never executed.

Expected: the job persists until it self-removes or the user removes it.
Actual: the job vanishes from `jobs.json` (and from `hermes cron list`) without ever running.

## Root-cause hypothesis

The gateway's in-process cron scheduler keeps an in-memory view of jobs (`cron/scheduler.py`), while the CLI and the `cronjob` tool write/read `jobs.json` (`cron/jobs.py::_current_cron_store`, profile-resolved). On a scheduler tick or state reconciliation the gateway persists its own in-memory list back to `jobs.json`, **clobbering any job that exists only on disk** (CLI-created) — and for tool-created `no_agent` jobs, the create path appears to return the job object without actually registering/persisting it. Related: #60014 (module-level `JOBS_FILE` caching defeats test isolation / real jobs leaking), #75607 (feature proposal to separate declarative definitions from volatile execution state), #61031 / #62341 (no-agent runs invisible in the desktop panel).

## Suggested investigation

- `cron/jobs.py` — create/persist path for `no_agent` jobs (does the `cronjob` tool create register the job in the scheduler's in-memory list before saving?).
- `cron/scheduler.py` — the tick/reconcile path that rewrites `jobs.json` from in-memory state; it should merge rather than replace, or persist on-disk changes.
- Reproduce with a minimal test: CLI-create a `no_agent` job, tick the scheduler (`hermes cron tick`), observe `jobs.json`.

## Impact

Any `--no-agent` watchdog/alert job (the documented pattern for silent script-based monitoring) is unreliable on a running gateway: it can disappear before its first fire, with no error surfaced anywhere (no execution record, no delivery error).

items.title: Telegram adapter hangs forever on initialize() inside hermes gateway run (deadlock in _await_with_thread_deadline)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
# Telegram adapter hangs forever on `initialize()` inside `hermes gateway run` (deadlock in `_await_with_thread_deadline`)

## Summary

`hermes gateway run` with Telegram enabled never finishes connecting. It logs
`[Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` and then hangs indefinitely
— the `_await_with_thread_deadline` wrapper never returns, neither via the
`initialize()` task completing nor via its own timeout firing. The bot never
receives messages.

Everything *around* the adapter works: network egress, the bot token, and even
`python-telegram-bot` `Application.initialize()` in isolation (0.6–0.7s). The
hang is specific to the adapter's connect wrapper when run inside the gateway
event loop.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), source at git HEAD `0957277`
  (`refactor(skills): move polymarket to optional-skills/finance`, pulled via `hermes update`)
- OS: Linux (kernel 7.0.0-27-generic), systemd user session active
- Python 3.11.15 (venv at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`)
- `python-telegram-bot==22.6`, `httpx==0.28.1`
- Installed the messaging extra explicitly: `uv pip install "python-telegram-bot[webhooks]==22.6"` into the Hermes venv
- Provider: `nous` (OAuth); Telegram token from @BotFather, `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` set, `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=false`

## Reproduction

1. Put a valid `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in `~/.hermes/.env`
2. `hermes gateway run` (foreground or as a systemd user service — same result)
3. Observe logs:

```
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```

4. The process stays alive forever at `attempt 1/8`. With
   `HERMES_TELEGRAM_INIT_TIMEOUT=5` set, it still hangs >100s without ever
   logging `timed out — retrying`, proving the wrapper's timeout never fires.

## Evidence that the failure is in the wrapper, not in Telegram/PTB/network

All run from the same venv / same machine / same token:

- `curl https://api.telegram.org` → `HTTP 302` in 0.6s
- `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getMe` → `{"ok":true,"result":{"username":"dantas_hermesbot",...}}`
- `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates` → `{"ok":true,"result":[]}` in <12s
- Isolated PTB `Application.initialize()` (defaults **and** with the adapter's
  exact `request_kwargs` — `connection_pool_size=512`, `pool_timeout=8.0`,
  `connect_timeout=10.0`, `read_timeout=20.0`, `write_timeout=20.0`,
  `media_write_timeout=60.0`) → `INIT OK` in 0.6–0.7s, `get_me` returns the bot

So token validity, TLS, DNS, and `python-telegram-bot` itself are all fine.
The hang only appears when `_await_with_thread_deadline` wraps
`self._app.initialize()` inside `hermes gateway run`.

## Suspected root cause

In `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`, the connect loop (≈ line 3890–3940)
calls:

```python
await _await_with_thread_deadline(
    self._app.initialize(),
    timeout=_init_timeout,
    on_abandon=lambda app=self._app: _shutdown_abandoned_app(app),
)
```

`_await_with_thread_deadline` (defined at line 97) uses a `threading.Timer`
watchdog that calls `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(_mark_expired)` to resolve a
`deadline` future, then `await asyncio.wait({task, deadline}, FIRST_COMPLETED)`.

When run inside the gateway's event loop, neither branch resolves:
- the `initialize()` task does not complete within the timeout, **and**
- the `threading.Timer` → `call_soon_threadsafe` deadline never causes
  `asyncio.wait` to return either.

The result is a permanent hang at `attempt 1/8` (the loop body never reaches
the `except asyncio.TimeoutError` / `except OSError` retry branches). Because
`initialize()` succeeds in <1s outside the gateway, the most likely culprit is
the interaction between the `threading.Timer` watchdog and the gateway's event
loop / supervisor (e.g. the loop thread the adapter runs on not processing the
thread-safe callback, or the `asyncio.wait` not waking on the `deadline`
future). Disabling the fallback transport (`HERMES_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS=true`)
and forcing `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS` did not change the outcome.

## Workaround that confirms the diagnosis

A standalone `python-telegram-bot` long-polling process (same venv, same token)
starts, authenticates (`getMe` 200), deletes any webhook, and polls
(`getUpdates` 200 every ~10s) with no hang. Wiring each incoming message to
`hermes chat -q "<text>"` and returning the output works end-to-end. This proves
the Telegram integration itself is healthy and the defect is in the gateway
adapter's connect path.

## Suggested fix direction

- Make `_await_with_thread_deadline` robust to the gateway's loop/supervisor:
  prefer `asyncio.wait_for(awaitable, timeout)` (which the docstring says was
  avoided due to `anyio` cancellation shielding) **or** ensure the
  `deadline` future is resolved on the running loop and that `asyncio.wait`
  actually observes it. A minimal check is whether `call_soon_threadsafe` is
  posting to the *same* loop object the adapter's coroutine is scheduled on.
- Add an integration test that drives `initialize()` against a mock/real
  Telegram endpoint inside the gateway's actual event loop (not a bare
  `asyncio.run` in a unit test), so this deadlock class is caught in CI.

## Config snippets (no secrets)

`.env`:
```
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=8895…BGr8          # valid, getMe ok
TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS=86998056525
GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=false
```

`hermes config get model.provider` → `nous`

## Impact

Telegram (and likely any platform adapter that uses the same
`_await_with_thread_deadline` connect pattern) is unusable via
`hermes gateway run` on affected environments. Users must fall back to a custom
polling script, losing the gateway's pairing/allowlist/cron-delivery features.

items.title: Slack channel directory resolves thread-qualified routing IDs individually — ~30 base conversations fan out to ~1.6k sequential conversations.info calls, blocking gateway startup for ~8–12 min

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

`gateway/channel_directory.py::_build_slack()` passes Hermes-internal thread-qualified routing IDs (`chat_id:thread_id`) directly to Slack `conversations.info(channel=...)`. Slack does not understand these composite IDs, so every such call fails, and the composite IDs also never match the base channel IDs returned by `users.conversations`.

In our deployment the completed directory had ~1.6k targets. All but ~14 were raw (unnamed), and every raw entry was a thread-qualified composite ID — together they represent only ~30 distinct base conversations. That turns ~30 necessary lookups into ~1.6k sequential API round trips with no base-ID dedupe, no build-level timeout, no negative cache, and DEBUG-only failure logging.

Because the initial build is awaited before the startup restore gate opens, affected gateway restarts blocked inbound processing for approximately 8–12 minutes. Four fully retained reproductions took approximately 671s, 638s, 484s, and 482s. One additional observed run took approximately 710s, but its complete log segment was not retained.

Related: #79044 reports the availability symptom, and PR #79060 bounds the startup build with a 30s timeout — but neither fixes this fan-out. It is a correctness issue (the lookups fail even with a timeout in place) and it also re-runs on the 5-minute housekeeping refresh, where `future.result(timeout=30)` only releases the waiting thread and never cancels the running coroutine, so slow refreshes can overlap.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Slack gateway long enough to accumulate thread sessions: a session store where most Slack targets are thread-qualified (`chat_id:thread_id`) across a small number of base conversations (ours: ~1.6k thread targets over ~30 base conversations).
2. Restart the gateway.
3. Observe: auth and Socket Mode connect in under 1 second, then no resolver progress at INFO level until "Channel directory built: N target(s)" appears ~8–12 minutes later.
4. Send the bot a Slack message during that window: it is queued ("Queued inbound message during gateway startup restore") and only answered after the build completes.

### Expected Behavior

- Name resolution keyed by (team, base conversation ID): at most one `conversations.info` call per unique base conversation (~30 here, not ~1.6k), reusing names already returned by `users.conversations`.
- The thread-qualified ID kept intact for routing; only the API lookup normalized to the base ID.
- The startup inbound gate not blocked by directory building — serve the cached directory, refresh in the background, or fail open on timeout.

### Actual Behavior

- Across five observed restarts on the same host with near-identical data, directory builds took approximately 481–711s and still left all composite-ID entries unresolved. These thread-qualified routing IDs are not valid Slack conversation IDs for conversations.info; complete log segments were retained for four of the five runs.
- A bounded read-only probe of 6 composite-ID calls returned `ratelimited` in 0.288–0.297s each. The Slack client has only `AsyncConnectionErrorRetryHandler` registered, so rate-limit responses fail fast, are swallowed at DEBUG level, and leave no INFO trace.
- When inbound messages arrive during this startup window, they remain queued until the directory build completes. In one retained reproduction, an inbound message remained queued for approximately 6 minutes.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Slack

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: this gateway runs against a workplace Slack workspace, and
`hermes debug share` (including the `--local` variant's output) would expose
logs containing channel IDs and message content. Sanitized log excerpts
(timestamps relativized, channel IDs redacted) and a full file/line-level
root cause analysis are included below. Happy to provide additional
redacted excerpts on request.
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.3

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)

Running checkout: 863e31318
Upstream HEAD at report time: 0957277f

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
(timestamps relativized to gateway start; channel ID redacted)
T+0s      INFO gateway.run: Starting Hermes Gateway...
T+0.4s    INFO [Slack] Socket Mode connected (1 workspace(s))
T+2m19s   INFO gateway.run: Queued inbound message during gateway startup restore: platform=slack chat=<redacted>
T+8m02s   INFO gateway.run: Channel directory built: ~1.6k target(s)
T+8m11s   INFO gateway.run: Drained 1 inbound message(s) queued during startup restore
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

1. `gateway/channel_directory.py:97-104` — session targets get composite IDs (`chat_id:thread_id`), which are valid as internal routing references.
2. `_build_slack()` (lines 372-381) collects entries whose name is still a raw ID and calls `conversations_info(channel=entry["id"])` with the composite ID. It never splits off the base `chat_id`, so the `api_name_lookup` built from `users.conversations` (lines 357-359) cannot match either.
3. The resolution loop is sequential, with no base-ID dedupe, no build timeout, and no negative cache; per-entry failures are logged at DEBUG only (lines 398-400).
4. `gateway/run.py:11385-11392` awaits this build before the startup restore gate opens.
5. Housekeeping (`run.py:26155-26192`) re-schedules the same build every 5 minutes. `future.result(timeout=30)` releases the waiting thread but never cancels the coroutine, so slow refreshes can overlap.

**Regression window** (same host, near-identical data — target count changed only ~3%):

- With a 2026-07-22 deployment of main (`11ae6bf0e`), `gateway/channel_directory.py` contains no `conversations.info` call at all. Raw entries simply stayed raw, and builds took 1.2–4.8s at ~1.55k targets.
- After pulling main on 2026-08-06 (`11ae6bf0e..863e31318`, which brings in `8685fea0ce` "fix(slack): resolve channel IDs to human-readable names", authored 2026-04-30, merged 2026-07-23), builds take 481–711s at ~1.6k targets, with the first slow build occurring within minutes of the pull.

This pins the blocking fan-out to `8685fea0ce` interacting with thread-qualified session target IDs, rather than to gradual data growth.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. **Correctness (the main fix):** resolve names by (team, base `chat_id`) only — conceptually `lookup_id = routing_id.split(":", 1)[0]`, preferably by keeping `chat_id` and `thread_id` as separate fields in the session origin. One `conversations.info` call per unique base conversation, fanning the resolved name back out to all of its thread targets, and reusing names already present from `users.conversations`. This alone reduces ~1.6k calls to ~30.
2. **Availability:** seed startup with the existing `channel_directory.json` and refresh in the background (complements the 30s bound in PR #79060).
3. **Housekeeping:** a single-flight lock plus real coroutine cancellation on timeout.
4. **Only then, if unreachable conversations remain:** a TTL negative cache keyed by (team, bot identity, base conversation ID), distinguishing `ratelimited` from `channel_not_found`. Raising concurrency before fixing the fan-out would only make rate limiting worse.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: fix(desktop): agent reactions persist but never paint live (message.reaction event not delivered to renderer)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Agent reactions (the `react_to_message` tool) **persist correctly but never paint live** in the desktop app: the `message.reaction` event does not reach the renderer, so the emoji only appears after the conversation is reloaded/resumed. Confirmed on the local-desktop and remote-dashboard topologies with the current `serve` backend.

## Repro

1. Hermes Desktop (current main, `serve` backend) → send any message.
2. Agent reacts via `react_to_message` (tool returns `success: true`).
3. The emoji does **not** appear on the bubble in the open window.
4. Close & reopen the conversation (or restart the app) → the reaction **does** appear.

## Verified

- **Persistence works**: `SessionDB.set_message_reaction` writes the reaction; the tool result reports the new reaction list. (Checked live: rows carry `display_metadata.reactions` with `author: agent`.)
- **On-load paint works**: the renderer reads reactions from the transcript on resume/reload — this is why step 4 shows them.
- **Renderer handler is correct**: `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts:1045` handles `message.reaction` with both legs — match by durable `rowId`, and a live leg that finds the newest optimistic message of the reacted role and stamps rowId + reactions (`findLastIndex(role === reactedRole && rowId === undefined)`, lines 1072-1089). Either leg should paint.
- **Emit chain exists**: `react_to_message_tool.py` → `tools/desktop_ui.emit` → emitter installed by `tui_gateway/server.py:_wire_desktop_ui()` (called unconditionally from `_start_notification_poller`) → `_emit` → `write_json` → session transport (rebound on the conversation thread, `server.py:9424`).

## What this means

The gap is in **event delivery** between the backend and the renderer in the `serve`-backend / desktop topology — the event is either not written to the transport the renderer's chat stream reads, or is dropped by the client stream. The tool swallows emit failure by design ("A missing bridge is not an error — the reaction is persisted either way and shows on the next load", `desktop_ui.py:75-77`), so there is no log line and no way to tell from the server side whether the frame was delivered.

## Suggested direction

- **Instrument the emit**: log (debug or warn) when `desktop_ui.emit("message.reaction", …)` returns `False` (no emitter wired) or when the frame's write path drops it, so a missed live paint is diagnosable instead of silent.
- **Trace the frame's route**: verify `write_json`/transport binding for `message.reaction` frames emitted from the agent-turn thread in the WS-served (`hermes serve`) topology — the event must land on the same stream the renderer's `gateway-event.ts` switch consumes (i.e. the session's message stream), not a side channel the client ignores.
- If delivery is confirmed broken only on `serve` (vs the legacy dashboard spawn), align the emitter wiring with the gate fix in #80659 (same `HERMES_DESKTOP`/`HERMES_SESSION_SOURCE=desktop` family of serve-vs-legacy drift).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) + current main; desktop renderer built from current `apps/desktop`
- Topologies observed: local desktop app and remote client → shared dashboard/gateway
- First observed 2026-08-06; reproducible across both directions (agent ❤️/😂/🔥/🤔, multiple sessions)

Related: #80259 / #80659 (tool gating), #80670 / #80675 (RPC write-key resolution).

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop “Show earlier messages” disappears before reaching the true session start

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

In Hermes Desktop, older conversation history can become unreachable after switching to a long or compressed session.

Scrolling upward reaches the top of the currently materialized segment rather than loading more history automatically. A **Show earlier messages** control is sometimes present. Clicking it may reveal another segment, but it can disappear before the original beginning of the conversation is reached. Once it disappears, ordinary upward scrolling cannot recover any earlier messages.

This is more than a discoverability problem: the control is driven by the messages already loaded into Desktop, not by whether older durable display history exists.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Hermes Desktop with a long session that has undergone context compression.
2. Switch to another session, then switch back to the long session.
3. Scroll to the top of the visible transcript.
4. If **Show earlier messages** appears, click it and continue moving upward.
5. Observe that the control can disappear before the original first message is visible. Further upward scrolling does nothing.

The symptom is intermittent across sessions because short or uncompressed sessions do not cross the same history boundaries.

## Expected behavior

- The transcript should behave like a normal chat history: reaching the top loads the previous page while preserving scroll position.
- Loading should continue until the true beginning of the user-visible conversation is reached.
- A fallback **Show earlier messages** control should remain available while the server reports older display history.
- Switching sessions should not make previously accessible history unreachable.
- Renderer memory limits must remain bounded for tool-heavy transcripts.

## Actual behavior

- Scrolling only traverses the currently materialized tail.
- The button may require repeated clicks, then disappears before the true session head.
- The button state indicates only whether more messages exist in the current client array/window; it does not prove there is no older durable history.
- There is no remaining UI path to request additional history after the control disappears.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: `v0.20.0 +21`
- Source/build commit: `01a1037d1e6d7b6eb96a786ef282c3aea4818194`
- Operating system: macOS 26.6
- Python: 3.11.15

## Root-cause analysis

There are two separate bounded windows, both derived from the transcript already loaded into Desktop:

1. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/index.tsx` resets `windowPages` to one when the assistant runtime/session changes.
2. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-window.ts` selects a weighted tail from the in-memory message array.
3. `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx` applies an additional DOM render budget. **Show earlier messages** disappears when both that budget and the repository window are exhausted.

The durable transcript loader can provide an incomplete source array for compressed sessions:

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:get_session_messages` resolves the requested session to the current resume tip, then calls `SessionDB.get_messages()`.
- `SessionDB.get_messages()` defaults to active rows only.
- In-place compaction preserves earlier rows as `active=0, compacted=1`; these are durable but excluded by the active-only read.
- Rotating compression can put earlier turns in parent sessions while the endpoint returns only the current tip.

The UI can therefore exhaust its incomplete array, set `olderAvailable=false`, and remove the button even though the user-visible conversation has an earlier durable history boundary.

A naive `include_inactive=True` change is unsafe because it would also expose Undo/Rewind rows (`active=0, compacted=0`) and can duplicate protected tail messages copied across compaction epochs.

## Suggested direction

1. Define a dedicated user-visible display-history projection separate from the model working context.
2. Add reverse/cursor pagination with a server-authoritative `has_more`/`before_id` contract.
3. Reconstruct compression lineage and compaction-preserved rows while excluding Undo/Rewind rows and generated compaction handoff summaries.
4. Prevent duplicated protected-tail messages across compaction boundaries.
5. Have Desktop automatically request the previous page when the user reaches the top, preserving scroll position.
6. Keep the existing weighted DOM windowing after server-side reconstruction to avoid Chromium renderer exhaustion.
7. Add regression coverage for uncompressed sessions, both compression modes, multiple compaction epochs, Undo/Rewind, repeated legitimate content, copied-tail deduplication, session switching, and large tool-heavy transcripts.

## Related issues

- #69640 requests bounded session loading and automatic older-message loading on upward scroll, but does not cover compressed display-history reconstruction or premature `has_more` exhaustion.
- #52816 covers older messages that remain in the client store but are outside the DOM render budget; its discussion explicitly leaves manual upward browsing unresolved.
- #80141 covers the earlier-message control being obscured by a sticky message, not the control disappearing before the durable history boundary.

No private transcript content or debug upload is included; the report is based on the deterministic source path and observed UI behaviour.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop self-update can corrupt the existing runtime on Windows

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

Hermes Desktop v0.20.0 on Windows can corrupt its own existing Python runtime when an in-app update fails.

This is more serious than an ordinary update failure.

In my case, Hermes Desktop was working before the update. During the update, the updater attempted to modify the existing `venv` in place. Windows file locks prevented several files from being replaced, including:

```text
venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography\hazmat\bindings\_rust.pyd
venv\Scripts\hermes.exe
```

The updater then continued/retried after the environment had already been partially modified.

The result was an incomplete Python environment. Subsequent update attempts could no longer start Hermes correctly because one of Hermes' own required dependencies was missing:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'
```

At that point this was no longer simply:

> The new version could not be installed.

It had become:

> The previously working installation was damaged by the failed update.

For a desktop application's self-update mechanism, I consider this a serious reliability problem.

A failed update should fail atomically and leave the previous working installation intact.

I am attaching the relevant redacted updater log:

`hermes-v0.20.0-update-failure-redacted.log`

The local Windows username has been removed from the attached log. The relevant update/error output is otherwise unchanged.

**Additional v0.20.0 compatibility feedback:**

Separately from the updater bug above, Hermes v0.20.0 still has not completed migration to the **MCP Python SDK 2.0 (`mcp==2.0.x`)** line.

I am specifically referring to the Python MCP SDK, not using "MCP 2.0" as a protocol version name.

I am aware this work is already tracked in #69931, so I am not reporting it here as a new MCP bug. I want to explicitly add user feedback that I believe this migration deserves substantially higher priority for an agent platform whose integrations increasingly depend on MCP interoperability.

[hermes-v0.20.0-update-failure-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30810019/hermes-v0.20.0-update-failure-redacted.log)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with a working Hermes Desktop v0.20.0 installation on Windows.
2. Start the update through the Hermes Desktop updater.
3. Allow the updater to update the existing Hermes Agent/Python environment.
4. During dependency replacement, a Hermes-related process or another process still holds files inside the existing `venv`.
5. The updater fails to replace files such as:

```text
cryptography\hazmat\bindings\_rust.pyd
venv\Scripts\hermes.exe
```

6. The updater retries after the environment has already been partially modified.
7. Hermes subsequently fails during startup/update with:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'
```

The attached redacted log contains the complete relevant sequence from the failed update attempts.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes Desktop updates should be transactional/atomic.

If an update cannot safely replace files because the current Hermes runtime, gateway, Desktop process, or another process is still holding them open, the updater should abort **before modifying the working environment**.

The expected behavior is:

1. Verify that all Hermes-owned processes that can lock installation files have exited.
2. Download and stage the new version separately from the currently working installation.
3. Verify the staged installation.
4. Switch to the new version only after installation succeeds.
5. If installation or startup verification fails, keep or restore the previous working version.

In short:

> **Update succeeds, or nothing changes.**

A failed update should never require a normal Desktop user to manually repair a Python virtual environment, reinstall dependencies, or reconstruct Hermes.


### Actual Behavior

The actual sequence was approximately:

```text
Working Hermes Desktop
        ↓
Start Desktop update
        ↓
Updater modifies existing venv in place
        ↓
Windows refuses to remove _rust.pyd
(os error 5 / Access denied)
        ↓
Updater performs another dependency operation
        ↓
cryptography uninstall metadata is incomplete
        ↓
Windows refuses to replace venv\Scripts\hermes.exe
(os error 32 / file in use)
        ↓
Updater retries
        ↓
Existing venv is already inconsistent
        ↓
Hermes CLI starts from damaged environment
        ↓
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'
        ↓
Further automatic retries fail with the same error
```

Relevant errors from the attached log include:

```text
error: failed to remove file
C:\Users\<redacted>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography/hazmat/bindings/_rust.pyd:
拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
```

Then:

```text
warning: Failed to uninstall package at
venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography-50.0.0.dist-info
due to missing `RECORD` file.

Installation may result in an incomplete environment.
```

Then:

```text
error: failed to remove file
C:\Users\<redacted>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\../../Scripts/hermes.exe:
另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 (os error 32)
```

And finally, repeatedly:

```text
File "...\hermes_cli\secrets_cli.py", line 22, in <module>
    from rich.console import Console

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'
```

This means the failed updater did not preserve the previously usable environment.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
I cannot provide a normal `hermes debug share` report after reproducing the failure because the update process leaves the Hermes Python environment unable to start correctly:


ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'


Running Hermes tooling from the damaged environment is therefore not reliable.

Instead, I am attaching the redacted installer/updater log containing the original update sequence and failure:


hermes-v0.20.0-update-failure-redacted.log


The local Windows username has been redacted before public upload.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 (x64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.20.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
See attached:


hermes-v0.20.0-update-failure-redacted.log


The most important sequence is:


Using Python 3.11.15 environment at: venv
Resolved 100 packages in 2.17s
Building hermes-agent
Built hermes-agent
Prepared 1 package in 14.64s

error: failed to remove file
...\cryptography\hazmat\bindings\_rust.pyd:
Access denied. (os error 5)

...

warning: Failed to uninstall package at
venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography-50.0.0.dist-info
due to missing `RECORD` file.
Installation may result in an incomplete environment.

error: failed to remove file
...\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
(os error 32)

...

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rich'


The `ModuleNotFoundError` then repeats on subsequent automatic update attempts.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Based on the updater log, the immediate failure appears to be caused by the updater modifying the same Python virtual environment that the installed Hermes runtime depends on.

The sequence is:

1. Dependency synchronization begins against the existing `venv`.
2. A native extension (`_rust.pyd`) cannot be removed because Windows denies access.
3. Another dependency operation proceeds.
4. `cryptography` is left with incomplete uninstall metadata (`RECORD` missing).
5. `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` is also still locked and cannot be replaced.
6. The updater retries using the now partially modified environment.
7. Hermes fails during import because `rich` is no longer present.

The architectural problem is therefore larger than the individual file lock.

Windows file locking is expected behavior. A desktop updater should assume that `.exe`, `.dll`, and `.pyd` files may remain locked and structure the update so that this cannot corrupt the currently working installation.

The dangerous part is the **in-place mutation of the active runtime before the replacement runtime has been successfully staged and verified**.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

I strongly recommend changing the Desktop update architecture so that updates are staged outside the active Hermes environment.

For example:

```text
Hermes/
├── versions/
│   ├── 0.20.0/
│   └── 0.20.1/
├── current -> 0.20.0
└── user-data/
```

An update could then:

1. Download a prebuilt Desktop/runtime artifact.
2. Install it into a separate version directory.
3. Verify required files and Python imports.
4. Shut down all Hermes-owned processes.
5. Atomically switch the active version.
6. Start the new version.
7. Automatically roll back if startup verification fails.

At minimum, if Hermes continues updating the existing environment in place, the updater should:

- terminate and verify termination of every process using the Hermes installation;
- test that critical files can actually be replaced before dependency mutation begins;
- maintain a recoverable copy of the existing environment;
- never retry an update using a venv that a previous attempt may have partially modified.

A one-click update should not expose implementation details such as `uv`, Python virtual environments, npm, Electron rebuilds, or Windows file-lock recovery to ordinary Desktop users.

**A one-click update button is not enough to make the update process one-click.**

For a Desktop application, the desired invariant should be:

> **Update succeeds, or the existing installation remains untouched and usable.**

Separately, for the MCP Python SDK 2.x migration already tracked by #69931, I would strongly encourage raising its priority and providing a clear compatibility/migration roadmap for Hermes Desktop/Agent users.


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: cron direct_api_call path has no TTFB/stale watchdog; cron runs hang indefinitely on a stalled non-streaming response; 600s inactivity monitor observed not firing

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-automation
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect CI, automerge, label sync, or maintainer automation

items.body:
## Summary

Cron-scheduled agent turns (`platform == "cron"`) are routed by `should_use_direct_api_call` onto the non-streaming inline `direct_api_call` path, which has **no TTFB watchdog and no response-completion stale detection**. The abort plumbing (`_abort_active_request`, #29507 lock discipline) is registered, but nothing ever invokes it on this path. When a provider accepts a request and then stalls (connection held open, zero bytes, no error), a cron run hangs until an external actor kills it. The only other bounds are the 1800s-default httpx read timeout (never reached in any observed incident) and the 600s job-level inactivity monitor, which was **observed to silently not fire** (958s idle, zero "idle for" log lines on any surface).

## Symptoms (observed 2026-08-05, cron runs against an OpenAI-wire relay)

- Three cron executions stalled on the same signature: request accepted, no bytes, no completion, no error.
- All three were killed externally (invoker terminal timeouts / session teardown), which also **orphaned the executions** (rows stuck `running` with dead owners until scheduler-start recovery).
- Same-window controls: identical or larger requests completed in seconds immediately before/after, same provider/model; a 256K-token streaming call completed in 7.7s **during** one of the stalls; gateway-owned cron executions on the same direct path completed 225/225 in the same window. The provider was healthy — the degenerate state is per-request.
- The 600s inactivity monitor (`HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`) demonstrably did not fire in the one stall that exceeded its threshold (958s idle, zero log lines anywhere).

## Mechanism

`hermes cron run` → conversation loop → `interruptible_streaming_api_call` → **`should_use_direct_api_call(platform=cron)` → `direct_api_call`** → inline non-streaming `chat.completions.create()`, with a single activity touch at call start and no per-chunk activity, no stale/TTFB timer, no interrupt-check loop. The direct path exists to fix the nested-pool deadlocks #62151 (cron) and #60203 (delegated children) — it correctly avoids the deadlock but silently dropped the streaming path's health machinery. `interruptible_streaming_api_call` has the full watchdog surface (per-chunk read timeout + stale detector + activity touches); `direct_api_call` has none, and a watchdog that can be silently defeated (or that never fires) is not a per-call hard deadline.

## Proposed fix (implemented and tested — patch available)

Two daemon `threading.Timer` watchdogs inside `direct_api_call`:

1. **TTFB watchdog** — no response headers within a context-scaled budget (default 120s, scaled up to 240s for >100K-token contexts, capped at 180s; `HERMES_DIRECT_TTFB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`/`HERMES_DIRECT_TTFB_MAX_SECONDS` to tune, 0 disables the TTFB phase) → abort + retryable `TimeoutError`.
2. **Response-completion watchdog** — no complete response within the non-streaming stale budget (the same `_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout` derivation the interruptible non-streaming stale detector uses) → abort + retryable `TimeoutError`.

Both timers only invoke the already-registered `_abort_active_request` (socket shutdown under the holder lock, #29507 discipline) — they never issue requests, so the inline / no-worker-thread property that fixes #62151/#60203 is preserved. A watchdog abort surfaces as a retryable `TimeoutError` (also bumped into the #58962 cross-turn circuit breaker), never `InterruptedError`, so the outer retry loop reconnects fresh. First-byte observation uses the request client's httpx `response` event hook, attached per-request and removed in `finally` (the client is cached for reuse).

Note: current `main` already carries a 15s activity heartbeat in `direct_api_call` (added after our base), which addresses the sibling symptom of false inactivity interrupts during slow-but-healthy waits. The watchdogs are complementary: they bound the transport-stall class (accepted-then-silent) with a hard per-call deadline independent of the inactivity monitor.

## Tests

New `tests/cron/test_cron_direct_api_call_watchdog.py` — 6 tests, all green against current `main` + fix (and independently re-validated 14/14 across the broader gate):

- TTFB watchdog aborts a stalled call and raises retryable `TimeoutError`
- Completion watchdog aborts after first byte
- Retry loop recovers a stalled call
- Happy path: no watchdog fire, hook removed
- TTFB phase disabled by env still has completion watchdog
- Env contract for the TTFB timeout derivation

## Patch

Single commit, PR-ready: `fix(cron): add TTFB + response-completion stale watchdogs to direct_api_call` — `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` (+221) + `tests/cron/test_cron_direct_api_call_watchdog.py` (new, 6 tests). Cherry-picked cleanly onto current `main` (with the heartbeat kept intact). Patch file available from the reporter; happy to open a PR from a fork if that's preferred.

## Notes for maintainers

- The fix follows the existing timeout env-var convention (`HERMES_STREAM_STALE_TIMEOUT` etc.); happy to move the new knobs into `config.yaml` if that is the preference for new settings.
- Open question from the RCA: the 600s inactivity monitor can apparently fail silently (958s idle, zero log lines, `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT` unset everywhere checked). The per-call deadline from this fix removes reliance on that monitor; an investigation of the monitor's non-fire would fully close the class.
- Secondary note for the relay operator: the opencode-go-style relay intermittently accepts non-streaming requests in the ~40-60K-input class and never completes them while the connection stays open (no error, no timeout), while streaming and other request sizes succeed — a per-request degenerate state observed repeatedly on 2026-08-05 (11:54–14:52 PDT).

items.title: Desktop client silently truncates session history on ordinary prompt.submit (truncate_before_user_ordinal) — unrecoverable data loss

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary
Hermes Desktop (remote gateway mode) sent `truncate_before_user_ordinal=2` on an **ordinary prompt.submit** — the gateway silently truncated the session from 296 to 52 messages and persisted the loss via `replace_messages`. 244 messages (2 days of work) were deleted from state.db with no confirmation dialog and no recovery path.

## Evidence (tui_gateway gui.log)
```
2026-08-07 02:13:44 prompt.submit: truncating session 42bb68b4 history 296 -> 52 messages (ordinal=2)
2026-08-07 02:28:59 prompt.submit: truncating session ceb7a961 history 53 -> 52 messages (ordinal=2)
```
Two identical `ordinal=2` truncations 15 minutes apart — consistent with a stale client attaching the parameter to an ordinary submit, not two explicit user rewind actions (user did not click rewind).

## Root cause candidate
`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` lines ~160-240: `truncate_before_user_ordinal` is honored on every prompt.submit. The code comments even acknowledge stale clients (`Stale clients can attach truncate_before_user_ordinal=0 to an ordinary submit`), but the only guard is against **empty** truncation (`confirm_empty_truncate`). A non-empty truncation (e.g. ordinal=2 → history[:user_indices[2]]) executes silently and destructively.

## Impact
- Unrecoverable: `replace_messages` DELETEs durable rows from state.db; FTS cleaned, no backup.
- 244 messages lost (session 20260801_035129_2b7361, days 2-6 Aug work).
- Also correlated with dashboard memory spike (replace_messages on a 152MB DB while dashboard was near MemoryHigh) → dashboard hang.

## Suggested fix
1. Require explicit client intent for any non-empty truncation (e.g. a `truncate_intent` flag or a confirm round-trip) — do not honor `truncate_before_user_ordinal` on ordinary submits.
2. Alternatively: soft-delete / snapshot before replace_messages (keep old rows with `active=0` or move to a backup table) so truncation is reversible.
3. At minimum: log a warning and require `confirm_nonempty_truncate=true` mirroring the existing empty-truncation guard.

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway RSS grows unbounded (full transcripts held in agent cache) — shutdown hang + SIGKILL every 4-7h under multi-session load

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

The gateway process (`hermes gateway run`) grows in RSS without bound under sustained multi-session load: full in-memory conversation transcripts held by the per-session AIAgent cache are never shed, and shutdown eventually hangs past `TimeoutStopUSec` and requires SIGKILL.

**Measured on Linux (systemd user unit, cgroup v2):**

| Date | Growth | Duration | Rate | Signature |
|------|--------|----------|------|-----------|
| 08-05 | 1.26 GB → 14.2 GB | ~7.5 h | ~1.9 GB/h | shutdown hang → SIGKILL → restart |
| 08-06 | 10.4 GB at restart | — | — | same hang signature (pid 862487) |
| 08-07 | 1 GB → 10.7 GB | ~4.5 h | ~2.4 GB/h | swap 2G full, available 0 B, Pss_Anon 11,047,828 kB / Pss_File 2,954 kB |

All growth is anonymous heap (`smaps_rollup`: Pss_Anon ≈ 11.0 GB of 11.0 GB total at incident). The systemd stop is SIGTERM → flush of bloated buffers under `memory.high=10G` throttling + full swap cannot complete within `TimeoutStopUSec=3m30s` → SIGKILL → `Restart=always` recovers. The leak recurs every ~4-7h under normal Discord/Telegram/cron traffic (165 sessions active/24h).

**Root cause chain (code):**
1. Per-session AIAgent cache: `_AGENT_CACHE_MAX_SIZE = 128`, `_AGENT_CACHE_IDLE_TTL_SECS = 3600.0` — hardcoded in `gateway/run.py:69-75`.
2. Each cached AIAgent holds `_session_messages` — the full live conversation including tool outputs. Code comment at `run.py:23560-23566`: "can be tens of MB with tool outputs (file reads, terminal output, search results) on heavy 100+-tool-call sessions."
3. Eviction is only time/count-based (1h idle TTL, 128-cap). There is **no memory-pressure-aware eviction**: hot-but-dormant sessions (a turn within the last hour) are never evicted and hoard RAM all day.
4. The FTS-corruption guard (`_select_cached_agent_history`, `run.py:5113-5132`) deliberately preserves the LIVE in-memory copy when the persisted transcript lags ("Persisted transcript lagged live cached history ... preserving live conversation context"). Correct amnesia-prevention, but it means a session's in-memory transcript is never shed even when disk persistence is merely slow (observed 3× on 08-06: disk 214→257 while memory 218→261).

**Why this is NOT closed by #48287:** #48287 ("Agent cache causes 50GB+ virtual memory leak") was marked `implemented_on_main` via the 06-08 fix (#41974) which released LLM client objects/httpx connection pools on eviction. That fix reduced the leak but did not bound the `_session_messages` transcripts themselves — they are still held for every cached agent, and there is still no pressure-based eviction. Our three incidents (08-05/06/07) all postdate that fix. Related: #62950 (unbounded in-memory caches), #62743 (TUI 7.4GB/8 sessions), #47848 (TTL config PR, unmerged).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway (Discord + Telegram, or any multi-platform config) on a Linux host with systemd user unit + cgroup v2 limits (MemoryHigh=10G, MemoryMax=12G).
2. Generate sustained multi-session traffic: several active Discord/Telegram threads with tool-heavy turns (terminal, file reads, web search) over 4-8h — normal usage is sufficient.
3. Observe RSS growth via `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup` Pss_Anon: climbs monotonically at ~2 GB/h until it approaches memory.high.
4. Restart the gateway while RSS is high: the SIGTERM flush cannot complete in 3m30s (throttled + swap full) → SIGKILL → auto-restart. Repeats every 4-7h.

### Expected Behavior

Gateway RSS stays flat (bounded) under sustained multi-session load. The in-memory transcript cache should shed agents under memory pressure (eviction), not only on idle-TTL, and shutdown should complete cleanly regardless of accumulated transcript size.

### Actual Behavior

RSS grows 1 GB → 10-14 GB over 4-7.5h (all anonymous heap); shutdown hangs 3m30s under `memory.high` throttle with full swap; systemd SIGKILLs; the cycle repeats every ~5h. In the 08-07 incident the host had 0 B available memory before the kill.

### Affected Component

- [x] Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
- [x] Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform

- [x] Telegram
- [x] Discord

### Debug Report

_(fill in after `hermes debug share` on next reproduction — incidents occurred on the live production gateway; log excerpts: gateway journal shows `Persisted transcript lagged live cached history` 3× on 08-06; watchtower per-tick log recorded the climb.)_

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.8) — also observed on Windows 10 (see #48287)

### Python Version

3.12.3

### Hermes Version

post-0.20.0 main (installed from source clone; leak predates and postdates the 06-08 #41974 fix)

---

### Proposed fix direction (for maintainers)

The codebase already has the correct eviction mechanism: `_evict_cached_agent` (`run.py:23374`) clears `_session_messages = []` and rebuilds from the persisted session JSON on the next turn — reload-from-disk is proven. The fix is to bound the cache under memory pressure:

1. **Configurable cache bounds** (`agent.agent_cache_max_size`, `agent.agent_cache_idle_ttl_secs`) instead of hardcoded 128/3600 — supersedes #47848.
2. **Memory-pressure-triggered eviction**: when the gateway's own anonymous RSS (Pss_Anon via `/proc/self/smaps_rollup`) crosses a threshold, evict LRU cached agents through the existing `_evict_cached_agent` path (bounded batches, active-turn skip, no in-place truncation of `_session_messages` — truncation drops the system prompt and races concurrent readers).
3. **Persistence-caught-up guard**: skip eviction for sessions whose persisted transcript is stale/divergent (same divergence signal the FTS guard uses at `run.py:5113`), so no unpersisted message is ever dropped.

Happy to contribute the patch with the 48h verification data (Pss_Anon telemetry proving flat memory post-fix) if this direction is accepted.
