items.title: A2A peers rejected by gateway authz under profile multiplexer (authorization_is_upstream not honored for secondary profiles)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
# Bug report draft: A2A peers rejected by gateway authz under profile multiplexer

**Hermes version**: 0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
**Platform**: macOS, launchd-managed gateway

## Summary

With `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, inbound A2A messages routed to a
*secondary* profile are rejected by the gateway's user-authorization layer
(`Unauthorized user: <peer> on a2a`, gateway/run.py:14334) even though the A2A
adapter declares `authorization_is_upstream = True` and the peer presented a
valid bearer token. The task completes immediately with an empty reply.

The exact same setup works when the profile runs its own standalone gateway:
the authenticated A2A peer passes authz and the agent processes the task.

## Expected

`A2AAdapter.authorization_is_upstream` (plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py:389)
should exempt authenticated A2A peers from the per-platform user allow-list in
multiplex mode exactly as it does in single-profile mode.

## Actual

Multiplexer log on every inbound A2A message to a secondary profile:

```
WARNING gateway.run: Unauthorized user: alpha (alpha) on a2a
```

The caller (`a2a_call`) receives `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with no text reply.

## Repro

1. Profile `beta` enables the a2a platform (`gateway.platforms.a2a.enabled`,
   `extra.port: 9901`), peer tokens in `A2A_PEER_TOKENS`.
2. Profile `alpha` configures `a2a_agents.beta` (url + bearer token).
3. Standalone: start `hermes -p beta gateway start`; from alpha,
   `a2a_call(agent=beta, ...)` → works, full agent reply.
4. Stop all secondary gateways. Set `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` on
   default, restart the default gateway. All a2a listeners connect under the
   multiplexer (`✓ a2a connected (profile: beta)` etc.).
5. From alpha, `a2a_call(agent=beta, ...)` → `Unauthorized user: alpha on a2a`
   in the multiplexer log; empty completed task returned.

## Additional findings

- In multiplex mode the per-profile `.env` `A2A_PEER_TOKENS` is NOT picked up
  by the secondary a2a adapters — all listeners start in "localhost-only" mode
  with no auth (SendMessage accepted without token). The multiplexer process
  only sees the *default* profile's env; moving the token list there restores
  `REMOTE (bearer auth)` and 401s on unauthenticated requests. Per-profile
  `A2A_*` env scoping appears broken for adapter construction.
- `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` (set in the default profile's env) does not prevent the
  gateway-level `Unauthorized user` rejection — consistent with the rejection
  happening in `authz_mixin._is_user_authorized`, not adapter trust.

## Suspected area

`gateway/authz_mixin.py` `_adapter_profile_for_source()` /
`_authorization_adapter()`: the adapter-flag lookup
(`_adapter_authorization_is_upstream(platform, profile=...)`) appears to miss
the secondary profile's a2a adapter in `_profile_adapters` — either the profile
isn't stamped on the a2a `SessionSource` before authz, or the platform key
registered by the (deferred-loaded) plugin adapter doesn't match
`source.platform`. Falls through to allow-list/pairing checks, which a
token-identity like `alpha` can never satisfy, then default-deny.

## Workaround

`GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` in the default profile's `.env` (blunt: disables
user pairing checks for all platforms in the multiplex process).

items.body:
# [Bug]: test_plugins_cmd fails on Windows with UnicodeDecodeError reading run_agent.py

## Bug Description

`tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py::TestNoAutoActivation::test_compressor_default_ignores_plugin` fails on every native Windows machine with a cp1252 locale. The test never reaches its assertion.

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f in position 47744: character maps to <undefined>
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On native Windows with a default locale (`locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` returns `cp1252`)
2. Run `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py -q`
3. `TestNoAutoActivation::test_compressor_default_ignores_plugin` fails with `UnicodeDecodeError`

Reproduces every time. Nothing about config, provider or session state is involved.

## Expected Behavior

The test reads `run_agent.py`, checks that a specific comment is absent, and passes. 39 passed.

## Actual Behavior

38 passed, 1 failed. The read raises before the assertion runs:

```
tests\hermes_cli\test_plugins_cmd.py:532: in test_compressor_default_ignores_plugin
    source = open(ra_module.__file__).read()
Lib\encodings\cp1252.py:23: in decode
    return codecs.charmap_decode(input,self.errors,decoding_table)[0]
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f in position 47744: character maps to <undefined>
```

## Affected Component

Other

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

Not attached. This is a deterministic test-suite failure with no dependence on config, provider or session state, and the full traceback and root cause are below. Happy to attach a `hermes debug share` if it would still help.

## Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

## Python Version

3.13.13

## Hermes Version

0.20.0

## Root Cause Analysis

`tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py:532` reads the `run_agent.py` source back as text:

```python
import run_agent as ra_module
source = open(ra_module.__file__).read()
```

`open()` in text mode with no `encoding=` falls back to `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`. That is UTF-8 on Linux and macOS, and cp1252 on a default US Windows install (GBK/CP936 on a Chinese one). `run_agent.py` is UTF-8 and contains nine bytes that cp1252 leaves undefined:

```
>>> import locale; locale.getpreferredencoding(False)
'cp1252'
>>> data = open('run_agent.py','rb').read()
>>> [(i,b) for i,b in enumerate(data) if b in (0x8f,0x90,0x9d,0x81)][:3]
[(47744, 143), (76016, 129), (76034, 143)]
```

So the decode raises and the test never gets to its assertion. It passes everywhere else, which is why CI stayed green.

This is the same class the `check-windows-footguns.py` rule and the #71014 read_text campaign have been working through, but in the test suite rather than in shipped code. #37423 covered the `gateway/run.py` instances and is closed. #79490 is the same fix for `tests/scripts/test_contributor_map.py`.

Two more tests read files the same way. Neither fails today, because their fixtures happen to contain only cp1252-safe bytes, but both are one non-ASCII character away from the same crash:

| File | Line | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_web_tools_truncate.py` | 52 | stored extracted web text, which is arbitrary content from the internet |
| `tests/stress/test_atypical_scenarios.py` | 739 | worker task ids |

`scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` additionally flags nine bare `write_text` calls in `test_plugins_cmd.py` and two bare `open(..., "w")` calls in `test_atypical_scenarios.py`. The write at `test_atypical_scenarios.py:708` is the one that pairs with the read at 739, so fixing only the read would leave an asymmetric round trip.

## Proposed Fix

Pass `encoding="utf-8"` explicitly, and read through `Path.read_text` rather than `open(...).read()` so the handle is closed rather than left to the garbage collector. An open handle blocks tmpdir cleanup on Windows, which is its own class of test flake.

Scoped to the three files above, which are then clean under `check-windows-footguns.py`.

items.title: [Bug] macOS: orphaned `hermes serve` backends accumulate across repeated desktop restarts
items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, repeatedly quitting and relaunching the Hermes desktop app causes `hermes serve` backend processes to accumulate. Each app relaunch spawns a fresh `serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`, but older serve processes are not always reaped, so they linger as orphans holding memory and degrading system performance.

**Affected surface:** Hermes Desktop (Electron) on macOS. Observed building **8 orphaned serves** over one morning of restarts (5 of them were pure memory consumers with no listen socket / 0 connections).

## Expected behaviour

At most **one** `serve` backend (+ the optional launchd `gateway`) should be alive after an app relaunch. Quitting/relaunching the app must not leak an increasing number of orphaned `serve` processes with no owner.

## Actual behaviour

Over a session with several relaunches, these accumulated (all verified via `ps` + `lsof`):

- **8 orphaned `hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1` processes**, back-to-back start times (10:51 → 12:32, each matching one app relaunch),
- Only the newest had a listen socket **and** a live ESTABLISHED connection from the desktop Electron window;
- 3 had a listen socket; **5 were fully zombie** (no listen, 0 connections) — pure memory.
- The `gateway run` (launchctl) was the only other expected process.

The app kept working (the current window held a connection), but the stale processes consumed RAM until the machine felt sluggish.

## Root cause (traced in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`)

The desktop only stops the backends it *remembers*, and macOS closing the last window deliberately does **not** trigger quit:

1. **`window-all-closed` (main.ts:12028) on macOS keeps the process alive in the Dock** — it does NOT call `app.quit()` on `darwin` (only on non-darwin or during a hand-off). So closing windows leaves the backend running — correct by design.
2. **On a real quit, `before-quit` (main.ts:12024-12025) only stops:**
   - `stopBackendChild(backendConnectionState.getProcess())` — the **single** backend the current Electron connection state recorded,
   - `stopAllPoolBackends()` — backends in the spawn pool.
   There is **no** sweeper that scans running `hermes serve` processes and reaps the ones with **no live owner** (no ESTABLISHED connection from a Hermes desktop window).
3. When a relaunch/reconnect/profile-switch spawns a fresh backend, the old entry's owner (`backendConnectionState.getProcess()`) is `invalidate()`d, and the spawn's `kill('SIGTERM')` is **fire-and-forget** (Node `child.kill` returns immediately; it does not wait). macOS serves often **ignore SIGTERM** (verified: rest submit SIGTERM, process stays). Once that happens, no code path later knows about or reaps that serve — it becomes ownerless.
4. Because window-close ≠ quit on macOS, the escape rate rises with relaunch frequency (update → relaunch, reconnect, quick restart) — matching what the user saw.

## Reproduction steps

1. On macOS, relaunch Hermes desktop several times in a row, ideally with any of: reconnect via connection-config, profile switch, or a quick `Cmd+Q` → reopen.
2. After each relaunch:
   ```bash
   ps -Ao lstart=,command= | grep -E "hermes_cli\.main serve --host"
   ```
   Count grows with each relaunch; start times back-to-back.
3. To confirm an orphan (not the live backend), find which serve the window actually talks to:
   ```bash
   lsof -Pan -iTCP -sTCP:ESTABLISHED | grep -iE "Hermes|python"
   # Python<->Hermes(ESTABLISHED) is the LIVE serve. All other serve PIDs should be dead.
   ```

## Evidence

- 8 orphan serves, start times spanning ~1.5 h, matching individual app relaunches.
- `lsof -Pan -p <pid> -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN`: 3/8 listening; `lsof -Pan -p <pid> -iTCP | grep -c ESTABLISHED`: **exactly one** shows the desktop-window connection; the rest `0`.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin), arm64
- Hermes Desktop app (Electron)
- `hermes serve` launched from local `venv` under `HERMES_HOME`

## Suggested fix (whole bug class)

Add an **owner-aware sweep** at (a) new-backend spawn and (b) real quit: enumerate all `python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1` processes for this `HERMES_HOME`, and stop every one that has **no** ESTABLISHED connection from a Hermes desktop window. This fixes the whole class ("orphaned serves grow on churn"), not just a one-off.

Also: the desktop spawns the backend with `stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe']` — **not `detached`** — and on macOS a plain `SIGTERM` is the documented teardown, but it is fire-and-forget and a serve that ignores SIGTERM escapes. Consider a SIGTERM → SIGKILL grace window in `stopBackendChild` on POSIX too (currently only Windows tree-kills via `forceKillProcessTree`).

items.title: [Windows/Desktop] In-app update fails with WinError 5 (Permission Denied) due to Hermes-managed Node locking

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Describe the bug
On Windows, attempting to update Hermes via the Desktop App's 1-click update button consistently fails with a `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` pointing to `%HERMES_HOME%\node\npm.cmd`.

### Root Cause
This is an architectural lock issue introduced by the new **Hermes-managed Node** feature.
1. The Hermes desktop app relies on the managed Node.js environment located at `AppData\Local\hermes\node` to run.
2. When the user clicks update from within the GUI, the updater script attempts to verify, rebuild, or upgrade this managed Node environment.
3. Because the Electron/Node processes are actively executing from this directory, Windows enforces strict file locks. Any attempt by the update script to touch `npm.cmd` or overwrite the Node tree is immediately rejected by the OS with `WinError 5`.

### Impact
This completely breaks the seamless 1-click update experience for Windows users. They are forced to:
1. Completely shut down the desktop app.
2. Manually kill any lingering background `node.exe` processes via Task Manager / `taskkill`.
3. Open an external terminal (e.g., PowerShell) and run `hermes update`.

### Expected behavior
The updater needs a Windows-safe mechanism for self-updating the active Node runtime. Possible solutions:
- Use a detached bootstrap/updater process that guarantees the desktop app and all Node subprocesses are completely terminated *before* touching the `%HERMES_HOME%\node` directory.
- Download the new Node tree to a side-by-side temporary directory and perform an atomic swap only upon the next cold start.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 10 / 11
- Surface: Hermes Desktop App
- Version: `0.19.0` / `0.20.0`

items.body:
# Issue Report — Background review / /refine creates duplicate skills instead of updating existing umbrellas

**Date:** 2026-08-07
**Reporter:** Glitch (Carlos's Hermes agent on WSL/KATE)
**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Severity:** Low-Medium (agent self-improvement hygiene — duplicates pollute the skill corpus and split future retrieval)

## Summary

The `/refine` slash command and the automatic post-turn background review create NEW skills even when one or more existing skills already cover the exact same class, despite the review prompt explicitly instructing a preference order that puts UPDATE before CREATE. In a single day, three near-identical skills were created for the same topic (head-to-head LLM benchmarking) by: (a) an automatic post-turn review fork, and (b) a manual `/refine`.

## Evidence

### 1. The review prompt already instructs dedup (code is correct)

`agent/background_review.py` (lines ~207-254) gives the review LLM this preference order:

1. UPDATE A CURRENTLY-LOADED SKILL (if it covers the territory, PATCH it first)
2. UPDATE AN EXISTING UMBRELLA (via skills_list + skill_view)
3. ADD A SUPPORT FILE under an existing umbrella
4. CREATE A NEW CLASS-LEVEL UMBRELLA SKILL **when no existing skill covers the class**

The prompt also says "prefer the earliest action that fits" and requires the name to be class-level, not a session artifact.

### 2. Three duplicate skills created the same day for the same class

| Skill | Path | Born (dir ctime) | Creator |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model-head-to-head-benchmarks` | `~/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/model-head-to-head-benchmarks/` | 2026-08-07 00:55:11 | Automatic post-turn review fork (no curator run that day, no manual /refine at that time) |
| `llm-head-to-head-benchmarks` | `~/.hermes/skills/software-development/llm-head-to-head-benchmarks/` | 2026-08-07 (same day) | Unknown (same-day) |
| `model-head-to-head-benchmark` | `~/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/model-head-to-head-benchmark/` | 2026-08-07 ~02:49 | Manual `/refine` by user |

All three cover the same task class ("compare two LLMs head-to-head fairly") with overlapping content (fairness contract, delegation pinning, pitfalls).

### 3. The automatic review fork is the confirmed creator of the first duplicate

- Skill dir birth time: 00:55:11 — immediately after benchmark round 3 finished (delegation batch completed 00:53:33).
- Gateway log shows a `response ready` at 00:55:32 (2 API calls, 2180 chars) for the same session — agent-side activity not persisted as messages in the main session DB.
- `state.db sessions` shows NO background-review child session for that window; the only child sessions are the benchmark subagents (parent = main session).
- No curator runs that day (curator log dirs are from Aug 3-4).
- Conclusion: the automatic post-turn review (`_spawn_background_review` / `spawn_background_review_thread`) ran in a daemon thread with `skip_memory=True`, created the skill, and its session/transcript is not persisted to the main session DB — so the user cannot see what it did, and it did not see existing skills.

### 4. The manual /refine also skipped dedup

The user ran `/refine` at ~02:49. It created `model-head-to-head-benchmark` (singular) even though the two earlier skills existed. The review fork inherits `enabled_toolsets` from the parent agent, so `skills_list`/`skill_view` were available — the prompt required using them before CREATE.

### 5. No runtime/log evidence of a code-level failure

- The prompt is correct.
- The tools are available.
- The failure is behavioral: the review LLM (gpt-5.6-terra-family) took the CREATE shortcut twice.

## Root cause hypothesis

The review LLM does not reliably execute the `skills_list` → `skill_view` → patch-or-create decision, even when instructed. Two occurrences in one day on the same class suggests it is a systematic bias, not a one-off: "create something new" is a stronger action tendency than "find and patch existing", especially under context pressure. The post-turn automatic trigger makes it worse because its transcript is invisible to the user (not persisted to the main session).

## Suggested fix directions (for maintainers)

1. **Add a hard pre-create gate in `background_review.py`:** before any `skill_manage create`, require the review to have called `skills_list` and `skill_view` on the top N candidates, and to name the existing skill it considered and rejected. (Prompt-level requirement is insufficient — enforce at the tool-call level.)
2. **Persist review transcripts:** background-review forks should write their transcript/session to the session DB (even with `skip_memory=True`) so users can audit what the automatic review did.
3. **Deduplicate on name similarity:** before create, fuzzy-match against existing skill names/descriptions (e.g. Levenshtein/embedding on the description field) and refuse or warn on near-duplicate class coverage.
4. **Report duplicates to the user:** if two overlapping skills are detected after a review, surface a consolidation suggestion instead of silently adding a third.

## Reproduction

1. Have a session where a non-trivial technique class is covered by an existing skill.
2. Run `/refine` (or let a post-turn auto-review fire).
3. Observe that a new skill is created even though `skills_list` shows an existing skill with the same description trigger.

## Cleanup performed by reporter

The three duplicates were consolidated into `model-head-to-head-benchmarks` (which had the most complete support files: templates + references). The other two were deleted with `absorbed_into`. Files were verified after cleanup (1 skill, 3 references, 1 template, frontmatter valid).

## Files referenced

- `agent/background_review.py` — review prompt (preference order lines ~207-254), `spawn_background_review_thread`, `skip_memory=True` fork (line ~800)
- `gateway/slash_commands.py` `_handle_refine_command` (lines 2847-2889)
- `run_agent.py` `_spawn_background_review` (lines 1794-1827)

items.body:
## Summary
Client-side argument-validation errors trip the shared MCP circuit breaker, making the Linear MCP server appear `unreachable` to ALL concurrent sessions for ~1 minute.

## Detail
When the model sends arguments that fail the Linear MCP tool schema (e.g. `Invalid arguments for tool list_issues: Invalid input`), `tools/mcp_tool.py` bumps the shared circuit breaker on any `isError` result. A validation error is a server RESPONSE — it proves the transport is alive — yet 3 consecutive bad-arg calls from one session open the breaker, and every concurrent session then sees `MCP server 'linear' is unreachable after 3 consecutive failures` until it recovers (~60s).

## Impact
- Shared, process-global breaker state: one session's bad args punish all concurrent cron sessions (board/reconciler/launcher all degraded for ~1 min per episode).
- Episodes repeat several times a day (observed 2026-08-06/07, e.g. 20:31Z, 07:41Z).

## Proposed fix
Classify client-side validation errors in the tool handler and do NOT bump the breaker for them; keep bumping on transport/auth/connection failures and server-side errors (heuristic substrings: `invalid arguments for tool`, `invalid input`, `invalid params/parameter`, `validation error/failed`, `unknown tool`, `missing required`).

This is tracked downstream in Vahor/ansible-configs PR #373 (patches the upstream image); this issue exists to monitor the upstream fix.

### Bug Description

SYMPTOM / 现象
--------------
On Windows (especially Windows Terminal / ConPTY), `hermes --tui` starts
fine, but after you type any command and press Enter, the TUI shows:
在 Windows（尤其 Windows Terminal / ConPTY）下，hermes --tui 能启动，

    gateway exited — recovering your session (any in-flight reply was lost)

The crash log (%LOCALAPPDATA%\\hermes\\logs\\tui_gateway_crash.log) shows:
崩溃日志中反复出现:

### Steps to Reproduce

On Windows (especially Windows Terminal / ConPTY), `hermes --tui` starts fine, 
but after you type any command and press Enter, the TUI shows:
gateway crashed.


### Expected Behavior

the workflow goes well as normal.

### Actual Behavior

I can start "hermes" command for using well.
And I ask hermes fixing the gateway crash in "hermes --tui".
The "hermes --tui" can be used good after AI(DS v4 flash) fixing.
This is the fix code below by AI:
And He said the issue will occured after "hermes update".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Fix: hermes --tui gateway crash on Windows
修复: hermes --tui 在 Windows 上输入命令后网关崩溃
============================================================

SYMPTOM / 现象
--------------
On Windows (especially Windows Terminal / ConPTY), `hermes --tui` starts
fine, but after you type any command and press Enter, the TUI shows:
在 Windows（尤其 Windows Terminal / ConPTY）下，hermes --tui 能启动，
但输入任意命令回车后，TUI 顶部弹出:

    gateway exited — recovering your session (any in-flight reply was lost)

The crash log (%LOCALAPPDATA%\\hermes\\logs\\tui_gateway_crash.log) shows:
崩溃日志中反复出现:

    File "...\\tui_gateway\\entry.py", line 357, in main
        for raw in sys.stdin:
    OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument

ROOT CAUSE / 根因
-----------------
`hermes --tui` spawns a Python gateway subprocess (tui_gateway.entry) from
the Node TUI frontend, talking over stdin/stdout pipes (JSON-RPC).  On
Windows, when the stdin handle is in a bad state (e.g. a ConPTY/console
handle misdetected as a pipe), iterating `sys.stdin` raises
OSError EINVAL (ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT) and the subprocess crashes.
Node TUI 前端 spawn 的 Python 网关子进程通过 stdin/stdout 管道通信。
Windows 上 stdin 句柄状态异常时，迭代 sys.stdin 会抛 OSError EINVAL，
子进程直接崩溃，TUI 随即显示 gateway exited 并自动重启。

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES / 修复内容
--------------------------------
Patches tui_gateway/entry.py with two idempotent enhancements:
对 tui_gateway/entry.py 应用两处增强（幂等，已修复则跳过）:

  1. `_stdin_handle_diag()` probe: logs the REAL identity of fd 0
     (GetFileType / GetConsoleMode / device path) into the crash log
     at startup and on crash, for future diagnosis.
     诊断探针: 启动时/崩溃时把 stdin 句柄的真实身份写入崩溃日志。
  2. Wrap `for raw in sys.stdin` in try/except OSError: an EINVAL read
     now records diagnostics + exits cleanly instead of dumping an
     unhandled traceback, so the TUI's auto-recovery takes over.
     主循环 OSError 容错: 崩溃从未处理 traceback 变为记录诊断+优雅退出。

USAGE / 用法
------------
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py                  # fix default install
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py --target PATH    # specify entry.py
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py --check-only     # detect only

AFTER `hermes update` / update 之后
-----------------------------------
`hermes update` restores entry.py to upstream and this fix is lost.
Just re-run this script.  `hermes update` 会把 entry.py 恢复为上游版本，
本修复会丢失，重新执行本脚本即可。

Verify / 验证
-------------
If a crash happens again, the log gains a `=== stdin read OSError ===`
section with the full handle diag line — paste that when reporting.
若仍崩溃，日志会出现 === stdin read OSError === 段+完整句柄诊断行。
"""

import argparse
import ast
import os
import shutil
import sys

# Default install path of entry.py / entry.py 的默认安装路径
DEFAULT_ENTRY = os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", os.path.expanduser(r"~\AppData\Local")),
    "hermes", "hermes-agent", "tui_gateway", "entry.py",
)

# Idempotency marker: presence of the probe function = already patched
# 幂等判据: 探针函数存在即视为已修复
MARKER = "def _stdin_handle_diag() -> str:"

# ---------- Patch 1: insert the probe after _install_sidecar_publisher ----------
# ---------- 补丁1: 在 _install_sidecar_publisher 之后插入探针函数 ----------
PATCH1_OLD = '''    server._stdio_transport = TeeTransport(
        server._stdio_transport, WsPublisherTransport(url)
    )


# How long to wait for orderly shutdown (atexit + finalisers) before
'''

PATCH1_NEW = '''    server._stdio_transport = TeeTransport(
        server._stdio_transport, WsPublisherTransport(url)
    )


def _stdin_handle_diag() -> str:
    """Describe the *real* identity of fd 0 on Windows.

    The TUI parent spawns this process with ``stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe',
    'pipe']``, so stdin is *supposed* to be an anonymous pipe.  On
    Windows, ConPTY / console-attach quirks can silently substitute a
    console (or ConPTY) handle instead, which makes CPython bind a
    different reader and ``for raw in sys.stdin`` fail with
    ``OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument`` (ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
    from ReadConsoleW on a pipe / ReadFile on a console input buffer).

    Dump enough evidence to tell those apart from the crash log:
    handle value, GetFileType (2=char/console, 3=pipe), GetConsoleMode
    (succeeds on *both* real consoles and ConPTY pipes — the telltale),
    and the resolved device path (``\\\\Device\\\\ConDrv`` = ConPTY,
    ``\\\\Device\\\\NamedPipe`` = a normal pipe).

    TUI 父进程以 stdio=['pipe','pipe','pipe'] spawn 本进程，stdin 理应是
    匿名管道。但 Windows 上 ConPTY/控制台句柄可能被静默替换进来，导致
    迭代 sys.stdin 抛 OSError Errno 22。此函数把句柄真实身份写入崩溃日志，
    用于区分: GetFileType=3 是正常管道; GetConsoleMode 成功则疑似控制台/
    ConPTY 句柄 (2=CHAR)。
    """
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        return "stdin diag: n/a (posix)"
    try:
        import ctypes
        from ctypes import wintypes

        k32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
        STD_INPUT_HANDLE = -10
        h = wintypes.HANDLE(k32.GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE))
        ftype = int(k32.GetFileType(h))
        ft_names = {0: "UNKNOWN", 1: "DISK", 2: "CHAR(console)", 3: "PIPE"}
        mode = wintypes.DWORD(0)
        cm_ok = bool(k32.GetConsoleMode(h, ctypes.byref(mode)))
        cm_err = ctypes.get_last_error() if not cm_ok else 0
        path = "?"
        try:
            bufsz = k32.GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(h, None, 0, 0)
            if bufsz:
                buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(bufsz + 1)
                k32.GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(h, buf, bufsz, 0)
                path = buf.value
        except Exception:
            pass
        raw = type(sys.stdin).__name__
        layer = type(getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None)).__name__ or "-"
        inner = type(getattr(getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None), "raw", None)).__name__ or "-"
        return (
            f"stdin diag: win32 h={h.value} GetFileType={ft_names.get(ftype, ftype)} "
            f"GetConsoleMode={cm_ok} (err={cm_err}, mode=0x{mode.value:x}) "
            f"path={path!r} layers={raw}/{layer}/{inner} fileno={sys.stdin.fileno()}"
        )
    except Exception as e:  # diagnostics must never take the process down / 诊断永不致命
        return f"stdin diag: probe failed: {e!r}"


# How long to wait for orderly shutdown (atexit + finalisers) before
'''

# ---------- Patch 2: wrap the main stdin loop in try/except OSError ----------
# ---------- 补丁2: 主循环包 try/except OSError + 崩溃时记录诊断 ----------
PATCH2_OLD = '''    for raw in sys.stdin:
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        try:
            req = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            if not write_json({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "parse error"}, "id": None}):
                _log_exit("parse-error-response write failed (broken stdout pipe)")
                sys.exit(0)
            continue

        method = req.get("method") if isinstance(req, dict) else None
        resp = dispatch(req)
        if resp is not None:
            if not write_json(resp):
                _log_exit(f"response write failed for method={method!r} (broken stdout pipe)")
                sys.exit(0)

    _log_exit("stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)")
'''

PATCH2_NEW = '''    # Diagnostic breadcrumb: record the *real* identity of fd 0 so a
    # Windows stdin read failure (OSError: [Errno 22] on ConPTY/console
    # handle substitution) is decodable from the crash log.
    # 诊断面包屑: 把 fd 0 的真实身份写入崩溃日志，便于事后解码。
    try:
        _diag = _stdin_handle_diag()
        with open(_CRASH_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as _f:
            _f.write(f"=== stdin diag · {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} ===\\n{_diag}\\n")
    except Exception:
        pass

    try:
        for raw in sys.stdin:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line:
                continue

            try:
                req = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                if not write_json({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "parse error"}, "id": None}):
                    _log_exit("parse-error-response write failed (broken stdout pipe)")
                    sys.exit(0)
                continue

            method = req.get("method") if isinstance(req, dict) else None
            resp = dispatch(req)
            if resp is not None:
                if not write_json(resp):
                    _log_exit(f"response write failed for method={method!r} (broken stdout pipe)")
                    sys.exit(0)
    except OSError as _e:
        # Windows: stdin reads can raise EINVAL (Errno 22) when the fd-0
        # handle is a console/ConPTY handle misdetected as a pipe (or
        # vice versa).  Record the handle identity, then exit so the TUI
        # parent can respawn — an unhandled traceback adds nothing here.
        # Windows 上 stdin 句柄异常会抛 EINVAL；记录句柄身份后优雅退出，
        # 由 TUI 自动恢复接管，未处理 traceback 毫无用处。
        try:
            with open(_CRASH_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as _f:
                _f.write(f"\\n=== stdin read OSError · {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} ===\\n{_e!r}\\n")
                _f.write(_stdin_handle_diag() + "\\n")
        except Exception:
            pass
        _log_exit(f"stdin read failed: {_e!r}")
        sys.exit(1)

    _log_exit("stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)")
'''


def already_patched(content: str) -> bool:
    """True if the probe function already exists (idempotent). / 探针存在即已修复"""
    return MARKER in content


def verify_syntax(path: str) -> bool:
    """Python syntax check after patching. / 补丁后语法校验"""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            ast.parse(f.read())
        return True
    except SyntaxError as e:
        print(f"  [X] Syntax check failed / 语法校验失败: {e}")
        return False


def apply_patch(path: str) -> int:
    """Apply both patches with backup + syntax-verify + rollback. / 应用补丁: 备份+校验+回滚"""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()

    if already_patched(content):
        print("  [=] Probe already present, nothing to do (idempotent) / 已修复，幂等跳过")
        return 0

    # Backup first / 先备份
    backup = path + ".bak"
    shutil.copy2(path, backup)
    print(f"  [i] Backed up -> {backup} / 已备份")

    # Patch 1 / 补丁1
    if PATCH1_OLD not in content:
        print("  [X] Patch-1 anchor not found (_install_sidecar_publisher tail).")
        print("      Upstream structure may have changed. File untouched. / 上游结构可能已变，未修改")
        return 2
    content = content.replace(PATCH1_OLD, PATCH1_NEW, 1)

    # Patch 2 / 补丁2
    if PATCH2_OLD not in content:
        print("  [X] Patch-2 anchor not found (main stdin loop).")
        print("      Upstream structure may have changed. File untouched. / 上游结构可能已变，未修改")
        return 2
    content = content.replace(PATCH2_OLD, PATCH2_NEW, 1)

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        f.write(content)

    if not verify_syntax(path):
        shutil.copy2(backup, path)
        print("  [X] Syntax error after patch, rolled back. / 补丁后语法错误，已回滚")
        return 3

    print("  [OK] Patched: probe + OSError tolerance written to entry.py / 修复已应用")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Fix hermes --tui gateway stdin crash on Windows / 修复 Windows 下 TUI 网关 stdin 崩溃")
    ap.add_argument("--target", default=DEFAULT_ENTRY, help="entry.py path (default: auto-detect) / entry.py 路径")
    ap.add_argument("--check-only", action="store_true", help="detect only, no modification / 只检测不修改")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    path = os.path.abspath(args.target)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        print(f"[X] File not found / 找不到文件: {path}")
        print(f"    Use --target to point at the correct tui_gateway/entry.py")
        return 1

    print(f"[i] Target / 目标文件: {path}")

    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()

    if already_patched(content):
        print("  [=] Already patched (probe present) / 已修复 (探针函数存在)")
        if not args.check_only:
            print("  [=] Nothing to do, exit / 无需任何操作，退出")
        return 0

    if args.check_only:
        print("  [i] Not patched (probe missing) — run without --check-only / 未修复，需执行修复")
        return 1

    return apply_patch(path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())



### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
The AI fixed, so pls read the Actual Behavior.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) 

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

AI:
问题已解决，且诊断数据齐全。整理一下结论：

    现状确认
    - 你的 TUI 会话（网关 pid 26232）从 10:38:56 spawn 起持续存活，提问后一切正常，没有再崩溃
    - 日志里最后一次活动是 10:48:08 的探针记录（stdin 状态正常），无任何新的异常
    - 我在实验期间创建的临时文件已全部清理；对 tui_gateway/entry.py 的改动保留着（下面详述）

    崩溃根因（已确认）

    hermes --tui 的架构是：Node 前端（ink）spawn 一个 Python 子进程 tui_gateway.entry 做网关，两者用 stdin/stdout 管道走
    JSON-RPC。崩溃发生在网关子进程主循环：


    for raw in sys.stdin:   ← entry.py:357
    OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument   ← Windows ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT


    即 Python 在 Windows 上迭代 stdin 管道时抛错。日志显示每次崩溃都发生在 TUI 启动后 37 秒~3分48秒——正是你输入第一条命令回车、网关处理 prompt.submit 的时刻。Windows
    Terminal (ConPTY) 下，Node 传给子进程的 stdin 句柄在特定交互序列后会变成无效状态，sys.stdin 迭代器触底就炸。

    为什么现在好了 —— 两层原因

    1. 主因：我加了诊断探针后发现，这类崩溃可以被"转化"——我给主循环包上了 try/except OSError，崩溃时不再直接抛未处理异常，而是把 stdin 句柄的真实状态（`GetFileType=PIPE,
    GetConsoleMode=False` 等）写入崩溃日志并优雅退出，由 TUI 的自动恢复机制接管（显示 "gateway exited — recovering"，重启网关、恢复会话）。你这次提问正好走的是正常路径，且
    ConPTY 句柄处于正常 PIPE 状态，所以完全没触发。
    2. 环境因素：排查过程中我 kill 掉了先前残留的 hermes/node/python 进程（进程列表里 10:22 和 10:29 那些），之前它们可能与其他会话竞争 stdin 句柄。

    当前代码改动（保留中）
    - tui_gateway/entry.py 加了两个改进（共 +110 行）：
      - 启动时/崩溃时记录 _stdin_handle_diag()：stdin 句柄的 GetFileType、GetConsoleMode、设备路径、IO 层——以后任何 Windows
    下再出现这个崩溃，日志里直接有决定性证据
      - for raw in sys.stdin 包进 try/except OSError：崩溃从"未处理 traceback"变成"记录诊断 + 干净退出"，TUI 自动恢复不再丢会话

    两个后续建议
    - 这个改动是本地补丁，hermes update 会覆盖；如果确认稳定，值得把这个诊断+容错逻辑反馈到上游（这是一个对 Windows 用户很有价值的修复）
    - 如果以后再遇到，崩溃日志 %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\tui_gateway_crash.log 里会出现 === stdin read OSError === +
    完整的句柄诊断行，直接把那段贴给我即可定位

### Proposed Fix (optional)

This is the fix code below by AI:
And He said the issue will occured after "hermes update".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Fix: hermes --tui gateway crash on Windows
修复: hermes --tui 在 Windows 上输入命令后网关崩溃
============================================================

SYMPTOM / 现象
--------------
On Windows (especially Windows Terminal / ConPTY), `hermes --tui` starts
fine, but after you type any command and press Enter, the TUI shows:
在 Windows（尤其 Windows Terminal / ConPTY）下，hermes --tui 能启动，
但输入任意命令回车后，TUI 顶部弹出:

    gateway exited — recovering your session (any in-flight reply was lost)

The crash log (%LOCALAPPDATA%\\hermes\\logs\\tui_gateway_crash.log) shows:
崩溃日志中反复出现:

    File "...\\tui_gateway\\entry.py", line 357, in main
        for raw in sys.stdin:
    OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument

ROOT CAUSE / 根因
-----------------
`hermes --tui` spawns a Python gateway subprocess (tui_gateway.entry) from
the Node TUI frontend, talking over stdin/stdout pipes (JSON-RPC).  On
Windows, when the stdin handle is in a bad state (e.g. a ConPTY/console
handle misdetected as a pipe), iterating `sys.stdin` raises
OSError EINVAL (ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT) and the subprocess crashes.
Node TUI 前端 spawn 的 Python 网关子进程通过 stdin/stdout 管道通信。
Windows 上 stdin 句柄状态异常时，迭代 sys.stdin 会抛 OSError EINVAL，
子进程直接崩溃，TUI 随即显示 gateway exited 并自动重启。

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES / 修复内容
--------------------------------
Patches tui_gateway/entry.py with two idempotent enhancements:
对 tui_gateway/entry.py 应用两处增强（幂等，已修复则跳过）:

  1. `_stdin_handle_diag()` probe: logs the REAL identity of fd 0
     (GetFileType / GetConsoleMode / device path) into the crash log
     at startup and on crash, for future diagnosis.
     诊断探针: 启动时/崩溃时把 stdin 句柄的真实身份写入崩溃日志。
  2. Wrap `for raw in sys.stdin` in try/except OSError: an EINVAL read
     now records diagnostics + exits cleanly instead of dumping an
     unhandled traceback, so the TUI's auto-recovery takes over.
     主循环 OSError 容错: 崩溃从未处理 traceback 变为记录诊断+优雅退出。

USAGE / 用法
------------
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py                  # fix default install
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py --target PATH    # specify entry.py
    python fix_tui_gateway_stdin.py --check-only     # detect only

AFTER `hermes update` / update 之后
-----------------------------------
`hermes update` restores entry.py to upstream and this fix is lost.
Just re-run this script.  `hermes update` 会把 entry.py 恢复为上游版本，
本修复会丢失，重新执行本脚本即可。

Verify / 验证
-------------
If a crash happens again, the log gains a `=== stdin read OSError ===`
section with the full handle diag line — paste that when reporting.
若仍崩溃，日志会出现 === stdin read OSError === 段+完整句柄诊断行。
"""

import argparse
import ast
import os
import shutil
import sys

# Default install path of entry.py / entry.py 的默认安装路径
DEFAULT_ENTRY = os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", os.path.expanduser(r"~\AppData\Local")),
    "hermes", "hermes-agent", "tui_gateway", "entry.py",
)

# Idempotency marker: presence of the probe function = already patched
# 幂等判据: 探针函数存在即视为已修复
MARKER = "def _stdin_handle_diag() -> str:"

# ---------- Patch 1: insert the probe after _install_sidecar_publisher ----------
# ---------- 补丁1: 在 _install_sidecar_publisher 之后插入探针函数 ----------
PATCH1_OLD = '''    server._stdio_transport = TeeTransport(
        server._stdio_transport, WsPublisherTransport(url)
    )


# How long to wait for orderly shutdown (atexit + finalisers) before
'''

PATCH1_NEW = '''    server._stdio_transport = TeeTransport(
        server._stdio_transport, WsPublisherTransport(url)
    )


def _stdin_handle_diag() -> str:
    """Describe the *real* identity of fd 0 on Windows.

    The TUI parent spawns this process with ``stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe',
    'pipe']``, so stdin is *supposed* to be an anonymous pipe.  On
    Windows, ConPTY / console-attach quirks can silently substitute a
    console (or ConPTY) handle instead, which makes CPython bind a
    different reader and ``for raw in sys.stdin`` fail with
    ``OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument`` (ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
    from ReadConsoleW on a pipe / ReadFile on a console input buffer).

    Dump enough evidence to tell those apart from the crash log:
    handle value, GetFileType (2=char/console, 3=pipe), GetConsoleMode
    (succeeds on *both* real consoles and ConPTY pipes — the telltale),
    and the resolved device path (``\\\\Device\\\\ConDrv`` = ConPTY,
    ``\\\\Device\\\\NamedPipe`` = a normal pipe).

    TUI 父进程以 stdio=['pipe','pipe','pipe'] spawn 本进程，stdin 理应是
    匿名管道。但 Windows 上 ConPTY/控制台句柄可能被静默替换进来，导致
    迭代 sys.stdin 抛 OSError Errno 22。此函数把句柄真实身份写入崩溃日志，
    用于区分: GetFileType=3 是正常管道; GetConsoleMode 成功则疑似控制台/
    ConPTY 句柄 (2=CHAR)。
    """
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        return "stdin diag: n/a (posix)"
    try:
        import ctypes
        from ctypes import wintypes

        k32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
        STD_INPUT_HANDLE = -10
        h = wintypes.HANDLE(k32.GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE))
        ftype = int(k32.GetFileType(h))
        ft_names = {0: "UNKNOWN", 1: "DISK", 2: "CHAR(console)", 3: "PIPE"}
        mode = wintypes.DWORD(0)
        cm_ok = bool(k32.GetConsoleMode(h, ctypes.byref(mode)))
        cm_err = ctypes.get_last_error() if not cm_ok else 0
        path = "?"
        try:
            bufsz = k32.GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(h, None, 0, 0)
            if bufsz:
                buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(bufsz + 1)
                k32.GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(h, buf, bufsz, 0)
                path = buf.value
        except Exception:
            pass
        raw = type(sys.stdin).__name__
        layer = type(getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None)).__name__ or "-"
        inner = type(getattr(getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None), "raw", None)).__name__ or "-"
        return (
            f"stdin diag: win32 h={h.value} GetFileType={ft_names.get(ftype, ftype)} "
            f"GetConsoleMode={cm_ok} (err={cm_err}, mode=0x{mode.value:x}) "
            f"path={path!r} layers={raw}/{layer}/{inner} fileno={sys.stdin.fileno()}"
        )
    except Exception as e:  # diagnostics must never take the process down / 诊断永不致命
        return f"stdin diag: probe failed: {e!r}"


# How long to wait for orderly shutdown (atexit + finalisers) before
'''

# ---------- Patch 2: wrap the main stdin loop in try/except OSError ----------
# ---------- 补丁2: 主循环包 try/except OSError + 崩溃时记录诊断 ----------
PATCH2_OLD = '''    for raw in sys.stdin:
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        try:
            req = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            if not write_json({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "parse error"}, "id": None}):
                _log_exit("parse-error-response write failed (broken stdout pipe)")
                sys.exit(0)
            continue

        method = req.get("method") if isinstance(req, dict) else None
        resp = dispatch(req)
        if resp is not None:
            if not write_json(resp):
                _log_exit(f"response write failed for method={method!r} (broken stdout pipe)")
                sys.exit(0)

    _log_exit("stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)")
'''

PATCH2_NEW = '''    # Diagnostic breadcrumb: record the *real* identity of fd 0 so a
    # Windows stdin read failure (OSError: [Errno 22] on ConPTY/console
    # handle substitution) is decodable from the crash log.
    # 诊断面包屑: 把 fd 0 的真实身份写入崩溃日志，便于事后解码。
    try:
        _diag = _stdin_handle_diag()
        with open(_CRASH_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as _f:
            _f.write(f"=== stdin diag · {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} ===\\n{_diag}\\n")
    except Exception:
        pass

    try:
        for raw in sys.stdin:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line:
                continue

            try:
                req = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                if not write_json({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "parse error"}, "id": None}):
                    _log_exit("parse-error-response write failed (broken stdout pipe)")
                    sys.exit(0)
                continue

            method = req.get("method") if isinstance(req, dict) else None
            resp = dispatch(req)
            if resp is not None:
                if not write_json(resp):
                    _log_exit(f"response write failed for method={method!r} (broken stdout pipe)")
                    sys.exit(0)
    except OSError as _e:
        # Windows: stdin reads can raise EINVAL (Errno 22) when the fd-0
        # handle is a console/ConPTY handle misdetected as a pipe (or
        # vice versa).  Record the handle identity, then exit so the TUI
        # parent can respawn — an unhandled traceback adds nothing here.
        # Windows 上 stdin 句柄异常会抛 EINVAL；记录句柄身份后优雅退出，
        # 由 TUI 自动恢复接管，未处理 traceback 毫无用处。
        try:
            with open(_CRASH_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as _f:
                _f.write(f"\\n=== stdin read OSError · {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} ===\\n{_e!r}\\n")
                _f.write(_stdin_handle_diag() + "\\n")
        except Exception:
            pass
        _log_exit(f"stdin read failed: {_e!r}")
        sys.exit(1)

    _log_exit("stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)")
'''


def already_patched(content: str) -> bool:
    """True if the probe function already exists (idempotent). / 探针存在即已修复"""
    return MARKER in content


def verify_syntax(path: str) -> bool:
    """Python syntax check after patching. / 补丁后语法校验"""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            ast.parse(f.read())
        return True
    except SyntaxError as e:
        print(f"  [X] Syntax check failed / 语法校验失败: {e}")
        return False


def apply_patch(path: str) -> int:
    """Apply both patches with backup + syntax-verify + rollback. / 应用补丁: 备份+校验+回滚"""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()

    if already_patched(content):
        print("  [=] Probe already present, nothing to do (idempotent) / 已修复，幂等跳过")
        return 0

    # Backup first / 先备份
    backup = path + ".bak"
    shutil.copy2(path, backup)
    print(f"  [i] Backed up -> {backup} / 已备份")

    # Patch 1 / 补丁1
    if PATCH1_OLD not in content:
        print("  [X] Patch-1 anchor not found (_install_sidecar_publisher tail).")
        print("      Upstream structure may have changed. File untouched. / 上游结构可能已变，未修改")
        return 2
    content = content.replace(PATCH1_OLD, PATCH1_NEW, 1)

    # Patch 2 / 补丁2
    if PATCH2_OLD not in content:
        print("  [X] Patch-2 anchor not found (main stdin loop).")
        print("      Upstream structure may have changed. File untouched. / 上游结构可能已变，未修改")
        return 2
    content = content.replace(PATCH2_OLD, PATCH2_NEW, 1)

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        f.write(content)

    if not verify_syntax(path):
        shutil.copy2(backup, path)
        print("  [X] Syntax error after patch, rolled back. / 补丁后语法错误，已回滚")
        return 3

    print("  [OK] Patched: probe + OSError tolerance written to entry.py / 修复已应用")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Fix hermes --tui gateway stdin crash on Windows / 修复 Windows 下 TUI 网关 stdin 崩溃")
    ap.add_argument("--target", default=DEFAULT_ENTRY, help="entry.py path (default: auto-detect) / entry.py 路径")
    ap.add_argument("--check-only", action="store_true", help="detect only, no modification / 只检测不修改")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    path = os.path.abspath(args.target)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        print(f"[X] File not found / 找不到文件: {path}")
        print(f"    Use --target to point at the correct tui_gateway/entry.py")
        return 1

    print(f"[i] Target / 目标文件: {path}")

    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()

    if already_patched(content):
        print("  [=] Already patched (probe present) / 已修复 (探针函数存在)")
        if not args.check_only:
            print("  [=] Nothing to do, exit / 无需任何操作，退出")
        return 0

    if args.check_only:
        print("  [i] Not patched (probe missing) — run without --check-only / 未修复，需执行修复")
        return 1

    return apply_patch(path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Bug report: Hermes Agent v0.20.0 - terminal/clarify tool results returning wrapped and sometimes wrong content

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), "The Herald Release"
- Python 3.11.15, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Deployment: self-hosted VPS (Debian 13), gateway running as a systemd
  --user service, Telegram platform
- `hermes doctor` reports fully healthy (no security advisories, config
  version v33 up to date, no deprecated keys)

## Symptom
Tool results (confirmed on `terminal` and `clarify`, likely broader) are
being returned wrapped in a literal content-block structure instead of
plain output, e.g.:

    [{'type': 'text', 'text': '{"output": "...", "exit_code": 0, ...}'}]

This looks like an internal Anthropic/OpenAI-style tool-result content
block that should be unwrapped by the harness before reaching the agent,
but isn't being unwrapped somewhere in the pipeline.

## Worse: wrong content substitution (not just wrapping)
Twice, a targeted `grep` for a short string inside specific small files
instead returned the **entire unrelated contents of a large file**
(`hermes-agent/AGENTS.md`, ~74,654 chars) wrapped in the same structure —
not a formatting issue, the actual returned content did not correspond to
the command that was run.

## Timeline / reproduction notes
- First observed today, several tool calls into a long-running session,
  after the v0.20.0 update was applied yesterday (previously on v0.19.0).
- A `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway.service` (done from a
  separate shell, since the agent is blocked from restarting its own
  gateway process) appeared to clear it temporarily — one clean,
  correctly-formatted result immediately after restart.
- The bug then recurred a few tool calls later in the same post-restart
  session, without any config change in between.
- Not correlated with memory ceiling (was at 2158/2200 chars when this
  started; cleaned up afterward, bug persisted).
- Not correlated with the separate/unrelated Slack token-expiry issue
  also seen in gateway logs around the same time.

## Impact
Not just cosmetic — the wrong-content substitution means tool results
cannot currently be trusted to reflect the command actually run, which is
a correctness/safety issue for any agent relying on terminal output to
make decisions (e.g. before touching production credentials/services).

## What would help
- Confirmation of whether this is a known issue in 0.20.0's tool-result
  serialization/output-handler path (terminal tool specifically, but
  possibly a shared code path also touching clarify).
- Any interim mitigation (e.g. a config flag, a package reinstall, a
  specific log format to watch for) while a fix is prepared.

Happy to provide full gateway logs / a fuller repro transcript on request
via the support channel.


### Steps to Reproduce

## Steps to Reproduce

I don't have a fully minimal, deterministic repro — the bug appeared
intermittently during a long-running gateway session, not on a specific
command every time. Best available reproduction sequence:

1. Run Hermes Agent v0.20.0 as a long-lived gateway session (systemd
   --user service, Telegram platform), updated from v0.19.0 the day before.
2. Continue normal multi-hour agent usage involving many `terminal` and
   `clarify` tool calls (mix of read-only commands: cat/grep/ls-equivalents,
   status checks, etc.) — the bug was not observed on the first several
   tool calls after gateway start, only appearing partway into the session.
3. At some point, tool results began returning wrapped in a literal
   content-block structure instead of plain output:
       [{'type': 'text', 'text': '{"output": "...", "exit_code": 0, ...}'}]
   instead of the expected plain JSON-ish result shape.
4. On two separate occasions, running a targeted `grep <short-string>
   <specific-file(s)>` returned the full unrelated contents of a large,
   unrelated file (hermes-agent/AGENTS.md, ~74,654 chars) instead of the
   expected small match set — same wrapped structure.
5. Restarting the gateway process (`systemctl --user restart
   hermes-gateway.service`, run from a separate shell since the agent is
   blocked from restarting its own gateway) produced one clean,
   correctly-formatted result immediately after restart, but the wrapping
   symptom recurred a few tool calls later in the same post-restart
   session — so a restart is a temporary, not permanent, mitigation.

I was not able to isolate a specific command, argument pattern, or
session length that reliably triggers it on demand. If it would help, I
can try to capture the exact tool-call sequence and timestamps from
gateway logs around the next occurrence and share that instead of a
synthetic repro.


### Expected Behavior

## Expected Behavior

Tool results (from `terminal`, `clarify`, and any other tool) should be
returned to the agent as plain, correctly-shaped output matching what the
tool actually executed — e.g. for `terminal`, a plain result like:

    {"output": "...", "exit_code": 0}

not wrapped in an internal content-block structure like:

    [{'type': 'text', 'text': '{"output": "...", "exit_code": 0, ...}'}]

That wrapper looks like an internal Anthropic/OpenAI-style tool-result
content block that the harness should unwrap before it ever reaches the
agent — the agent should never see its own transport-layer serialization
format.

More importantly: a `grep <string> <file>` command should return only the
matching lines from the specified file(s) — never the full unrelated
contents of a different file. Whatever content is returned should always
correspond to the command that was actually run, every time, with no
exceptions. That's the part that matters most here — the wrapping is
cosmetic-adjacent, but a command returning results for a different
command entirely is a correctness bug, not just a display issue.


### Actual Behavior

## Actual Behavior

Tool results were returned wrapped in a content-block list structure
instead of plain output, and on at least two occasions returned content
that did not match the command executed at all.

### Example 1 — wrapping only (content correct, format wrong)
Ran a plain `echo` sanity check. Expected plain output; got a
JSON-serialized result nested inside a content-block wrapper:

    [{'type': 'text', 'text': '{"output": "plain sanity check", "exit_code": 0}'}]

### Example 2 — wrong content substitution
Ran a targeted `grep` for a short string across two or three small,
specific files (expected: a handful of matching lines, or no matches).

Actual: the tool returned the complete, unrelated contents of
`hermes-agent/AGENTS.md` (~74,654 characters), wrapped in the same
content-block structure, with a note indicating the response had been
truncated at that size. This happened twice, on two different `grep`
invocations with different search patterns and different target files,
both times substituting the same unrelated AGENTS.md file.

### Example 3 — stale/wrong result surfaced via a different tool
Separately, our own gateway log (`~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`) shows a
`terminal` tool call at 10:55 UTC returning this as if it were real
command output:

    {"output": "---check tool result formatting config---", "exit_code": 1}

That string is not command output — it's a section-header comment/label
from a diagnostic script I had written, which should never have been
returned as if it were the actual stdout/exit-code of a real invocation.
This suggests result buffers or labels from unrelated tool calls were
being cross-contaminated into the response for a different, later call.

### Persistence across restart
A full `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway.service` (from a separate
shell) temporarily cleared the symptom — one clean, correctly-formatted
result immediately following restart — but the wrapping/substitution
behavior recurred within the same post-restart session a few tool calls
later, with no config changes in between.

No exceptions, stack traces, or error-level log lines were observed
correlating with the exact moments the bad results appeared — the
gateway log around those timestamps showed only unrelated, expected
entries (e.g. a separate/unrelated Slack token-expiry retry loop).


### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
## Debug Report

`hermes debug share` was not used for the public upload (its own warning
states it posts verbatim recent messages/prompts/tool-output to a public
paste service, which isn't appropriate given this conversation includes
real client/business data). Ran `hermes debug share --local` instead and
extracted the directly relevant evidence below.

### System info (from `hermes debug share --local`)
    version:          0.20.0 [1be70d63] (2026-08-05)
    os:               Linux 6.12.94+deb13-amd64 x86_64
    python:           3.11.15

    profile:          default
    provider:         nous-api
    model:            anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
    gateway:          running (systemd (user), pid 1295102)
    platforms:        telegram, slack
    cron_jobs:        2 active / 2 total
    skills:           110

### Exact log line reproducing the "wrong content" symptom
From `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`:

    2026-08-07 10:55:09,138 WARNING [20260724_181344_7cfc5e6d]
    agent.tool_executor: Tool terminal returned error (0.12s):
    {"output": "---check tool result formatting config---",
     "exit_code": 1, "error": null}

That output string is a comment/echo line from a diagnostic script I had
written a few tool calls earlier — it does not correspond to the actual
command executed in that specific tool call. This is the log-side
confirmation of the same symptom described above (wrong content returned
for a given tool invocation).

### Note on debug-share output size
`hermes debug share --local` itself produced a genuinely enormous log
dump (~1.6M characters, going back to July 24) rather than a reasonably
recent/scoped window, which made it impractical to review directly in
chat. Might be worth scoping `--local`'s log tail more tightly by
default, or documenting how to pass a custom line count.
```

### Operating System

Linux 6.12.94+deb13-amd64 x86_64 (Debian 13)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.20.0 (build 1be70d63, released 2026-08-05, "The Herald Release")

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

No exception or stack trace accompanies the bad output — that's part of
what makes this hard to catch. The tool_executor log line for the bad
result looks like a normal, well-formed success/error entry (see Debug
Report above), it just contains content that doesn't match the command
that was run. There's no crash, no non-zero process exit, and no visible
error surfaced anywhere in gateway.log correlating with the exact moment
the wrapping/substitution appears.

One clarifying note on the `[{'type': 'text', 'text': '...'}]` wrapper
described earlier: that's the literal shape of what appears in my own
conversation context when a tool result reaches me — I was not able to
find that exact wrapper string written out verbatim inside the plain-text
log files (agent.log / gateway.log), which store the underlying
already-serialized JSON payload instead. That's consistent with the
wrapping being introduced somewhere between the logged tool-result
payload and however it gets threaded back into my model context, rather
than at the point the tool itself writes its result.

Happy to capture a fresh, tighter log excerpt (with exact millisecond
timestamps) around the next live occurrence if that would help narrow
down which layer is responsible.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

I don't have a confirmed root cause — I wasn't able to complete a
reliable investigation, since the same bug interfered with my attempts
to read the relevant source. One lead, not verified:

A grep for the literal wrapper pattern (`'type':` / `'text'` content-block
shape) across the gateway/CLI source turned up a match in
`gateway/run.py`, but I could not confirm the surrounding code or
whether it's actually responsible — the follow-up read of that file was
itself affected by the same wrong-content-substitution bug described
above, returning unrelated content instead of gateway/run.py's actual
contents. I did not get a second, verified look at it.

Given the wrapper resembles an Anthropic/OpenAI SDK content-block object
(`[{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]`) rather than something Hermes itself
would construct by hand, my best guess (unverified) is that somewhere in
the tool-result-to-context path, a raw SDK message-content object is
being passed through instead of being unwrapped to its plain string/dict
value first — but I want to flag this explicitly as a guess, not a
finding, given I could not confirm it against the actual source.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

## Proposed Fix (optional)

No PR ready — I don't have a verified fix, since I wasn't able to
confirm the actual responsible code path (see Root Cause Analysis).

If the unverified lead above is right (a raw SDK content-block object
leaking through instead of being unwrapped), the general shape of a fix
would be: wherever tool results are threaded from the tool executor back
into the model context/conversation history, ensure the result is
unwrapped to its plain value (e.g. `.text` / plain string) before
storage or reuse, rather than passed through as the original SDK
message-content object — likely defensively, at the boundary, so any
call site that forgets to unwrap doesn't leak the raw object either.

Given the intermittent nature (clean immediately after a gateway
restart, recurring a few tool calls later in the same session) it may
also be worth checking for anything path-dependent on session/context
length or turn count rather than assuming it's purely tied to a specific
tool call — happy to help narrow this further with more logging if
that's useful once someone with source access can confirm the actual
site.

## Bug Description

A non-default Kanban board archived from the dashboard can reappear after the archive operation. From the dashboard, this makes the board effectively impossible to remove.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a non-default Kanban board in the dashboard.
2. Archive that board from the dashboard.
3. Keep the dashboard open, or refresh it after the archive.

## Expected Behavior

The archived board should remain archived and should not appear in the non-archived board list unless it is explicitly restored or recreated.

## Actual Behavior

The board can appear in the dashboard again after the archive operation.

### Operating System

 Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), Docker on WSL

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

v2026.7.20

## Root Cause Analysis

The dashboard archive endpoint calls `kanban_db.remove_board()`, which moves the board directory into `_archived`.

The dashboard live-events WebSocket keeps its board slug after the handshake and polls with:

```python
kanban_db.connect(board=ws_board)
```

`kanban_db.connect()` creates the board directory when it is missing and initialises its database. Therefore, a still-open WebSocket for an archived board can reconnect to the old slug and recreate an empty board directory.

## Environment

- Hermes dashboard
- Kanban plugin
- Dashboard live-events WebSocket enabled

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
# Windows: console windows flash on every subprocess spawn (serve / gateway / desktop backends)

## Environment
- hermes-agent v0.20.0 (observed on several recent versions)
- Windows 10/11 x64, Python 3.11 (uv-managed), running `hermes serve`, profile gateways, and/or the desktop app

## Symptom
On Windows, black console (conhost) windows briefly flash every time hermes spawns a subprocess without window-suppression flags. When hermes runs as a background service (`hermes serve --host 0.0.0.0`), as a messaging gateway, or from the desktop app's backend pool, these flashes land on the user's interactive desktop continuously — every tool call, every cron tick, every `git` invocation.

## Cause
On Windows, `subprocess.run()` / `subprocess.Popen()` without `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW` allocates a visible console window when the parent is a GUI or otherwise detached process. A scan of the tree (~3,800 Python files) finds ~678 `subprocess.run/Popen` call sites, of which ~610 pass no window-suppression flag (`creationflags`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, or the existing `windows_hide_flags()` helper).

Hot paths that make this *frequent* rather than occasional:

| File | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `tools/environments/local.py` | every local tool/environment call |
| `tools/terminal_tool.py` | terminal tool use |
| `cron/scheduler.py` | every cron job tick |
| `agent/coding_context.py`, `agent/context_references.py` | git/rg calls each agent turn |
| `tools/process_registry.py` | process tracking |

## Suggested directions (either works)
1. **Central (preferred):** route subprocess usage through the existing `hermes_cli._subprocess_compat.windows_hide_flags()` as the default on win32, or wrap the shared call helpers so flags are applied by default and callers opt *out*.
2. **Sweep:** add `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()` (or the POSIX-safe `creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0)`, which requires no new import) to call sites, prioritizing the hot paths above.

## Implementation caution (learned the hard way)
Calls that pass `**kwargs` where the dict already contains `creationflags` will raise `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'creationflags'` if a second literal is added — and this is a **runtime** error, not a syntax error, so it survives `compileall`. Any sweep should skip `**kwargs` call sites (their hiding typically already works via the dict) or merge into the kwargs dict instead of appending a literal.

## Verification approach used locally
After applying the getattr-based flag to ~460 call sites, `compileall` passes across the tree and a 5-minute window-enumeration watch on the desktop shows zero conhost windows from hermes processes (previously multiple per minute under serve + gateway + cron load).

Happy to share the scanner/patcher used for the local mitigation, or to open a PR with the hot-path subset if that is easier to review.

items.title: A2A outbound client tools (`a2a_call`, `a2a_discover`, …) never reach the agent's tool catalog

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), install method `git`, Python 3.11.15, Linux.

## Summary

The bundled `a2a-platform` plugin registers five outbound client tools — `a2a_discover`,
`a2a_call`, `a2a_list`, `a2a_history`, `a2a_orchestrate` — but they never appear in the
agent's tool catalog. This holds whether the inbound platform is disabled or enabled.

The **inbound** half of the same plugin works correctly: it serves the Agent Card, accepts
`SendMessage`, and returns `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`.

## Expected vs actual

`plugins/platforms/a2a/__init__.py::register()` states the intent explicitly:

```python
# 1) Client tools (outbound). Registering these even when the inbound
#    platform is disabled lets the agent call peers without exposing itself.
try:
    from .tools import register_tools
    register_tools(ctx)
except Exception:
    logger.warning("A2A: failed to register client tools", exc_info=True)
```

**Expected:** the outbound tools are available regardless of the inbound platform state.

**Actual:** they are never available. Notably, **no warning is ever logged** — the `except`
branch is never reached, because `register()` itself does not run.

## Root cause

### Layer 1 — platform plugins are deferred, so `register()` never runs

`hermes_cli/plugins.py::_register_deferred_platform` treats every `kind: platform` plugin as
a deferred load: it registers a loader with `platform_registry` and stores a placeholder
`LoadedPlugin`, but does **not** call `register(ctx)`. Its own docstring:

> *"The platform adapter module is imported only when the gateway / cron / setup /
> send_message path first asks the `platform_registry` for this platform."*

Since `register_tools(ctx)` lives inside that `register(ctx)`, the outbound tools are not
registered during `discover_plugins()`.

This is arguably correct for the *adapter* (that is the point of deferring), but it also
defers the client-tool registration, which has no reason to be tied to the inbound platform.

### Layer 2 — the toolset resolver would drop them anyway

`hermes_cli/tools_config.py::_get_platform_tools`:

```python
2253:    configurable_keys = {ts_key for ts_key, _, _ in CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS}
2254:    plugin_ts_keys = _get_plugin_toolset_keys()
...
2262:    has_explicit_config = any(ts in configurable_keys for ts in toolset_names)
2264:    if has_explicit_config:
2265:        enabled_toolsets = {
2266:            ts for ts in toolset_names
2267:            if ts in configurable_keys and _toolset_allowed_for_platform(ts, platform)
2268:        }
```

`plugin_ts_keys` is computed on line 2254 and never used in the filter on line 2267, which
only admits built-in `CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS`. A plugin-provided toolset listed explicitly in
`platform_toolsets` would therefore be dropped even if it *were* registered.

## Evidence

```python
from hermes_cli.plugins import discover_plugins, get_plugin_toolsets
discover_plugins()
sorted({k for k, _, _ in get_plugin_toolsets()})   # -> ['spotify']

from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_plugin_toolset_keys
sorted(_get_plugin_toolset_keys())                  # -> ['spotify']
```

`a2a` is absent. `spotify` is present because it is **not** a platform plugin, so it loads
eagerly — which is exactly the difference.

Asking the agent over its own (working) inbound A2A channel:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:9900/   method=SendMessage
  "Reply on one line: YES if you have the tool a2a_call, NO if you don't."
→ TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, artifact: "NO"
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. `hermes plugins enable a2a-platform`
2. Add an outbound peer under `a2a_agents:` in `config.yaml`
3. Restart the gateway
4. Ask the agent to call `a2a_list` or `a2a_call` → the tool does not exist

## Things that do **not** work around it

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins enable a2a-platform` | plugin `enabled`, tools absent |
| `gateway.platforms.a2a.enabled: true` | inbound server **does** start on `127.0.0.1:9900`, tools still absent |
| adding `a2a` to `platform_toolsets.<platform>` | no effect |
| adding `a2a` to `known_plugin_toolsets` | no effect |
| `hermes tools enable a2a` | `✗ Unknown toolset 'a2a'` |
| repeated gateway restarts | no effect |

## What does work

The inbound direction is fully functional: Agent Card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`,
`SendMessage` handled, tasks completed, conversations persisted under
`~/.hermes/a2a_conversations/`, audit written to `~/.hermes/a2a_audit.jsonl`. Bind safety
behaves as documented: with no token configured it listens on `127.0.0.1` only.

## Impact

A2A is effectively inbound-only in 0.20.0. An agent can be *called* by peers but cannot
*call* them, which rules out the `a2a_call` / `a2a_orchestrate` workflows the plugin
documents — the main reason to adopt A2A for multi-agent setups.

## Possible fix

Split client-tool registration from the deferred platform load, so `register_tools(ctx)` runs
during `discover_plugins()` while the adapter stays lazy. That matches the intent already
stated in the plugin's own comment. Line 2267 would also need to admit `plugin_ts_keys`
(or `_get_effective_configurable_toolsets()`) for plugin toolsets to survive an explicit
`platform_toolsets` list.

items.title: Desktop: turns aborted with misleading 'session storage could not be written' (compression-lock contention, no retry); sessions appear to vanish after disconnects

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Two related desktop-client problems:

1. **Turns are aborted with a misleading "session storage could not be written" / "often a full disk" error when a session is being compressed by another writer** — there is no retry, and the error copy blames disk space.
2. **Conversations appear to "disappear" after connection drops**: the tui_gateway marks every open session `end_reason='tui_shutdown'` on abnormal disconnect, and with `display.tui_auto_resume_recent` defaulting to `false` the client forges a fresh (empty) session on the next launch. All messages are intact in `state.db`; only navigation is lost.

## Symptom 1 — misleading fatal persistence error (core bug)

On a long session (hundreds of messages, context compression in progress), a running turn logs:

```
WARNING run_agent: Session DB append_message failed: Session '<sid>' is being compressed by another writer
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended with pending tool result (agent may appear stuck). Turn ended: reason=session_persistence_failed ... last_tool=terminal
```

and the UI shows:

> No reply: the turn was stopped because session storage could not be written (the transcript would have been lost on restart). This is often a full disk — free some space (or fix state.db permissions)

Disk was **not** full (600G+ free); `state.db` integrity was `ok` and writable.

**Root cause:** `hermes_state._check_transcript_write_guards` raises `SessionCompressionInProgressError` when a different writer holds the session's compression lock. The conversation loop treats the append failure as fatal and aborts the whole turn (`session_persistence_failed`), discarding tool results in flight. The lock is legitimate (the holder is mid-compression, TTL 300s) and transient — the append should wait/retry with a bounded backoff instead of killing the turn.

Also, the error copy ("often a full disk") is actively misleading here — it should mention the compression lock when that is the cause.

## Symptom 2 — "disappeared" conversations (UX gap)

- Desktop app connection drops are frequent (abnormal WS closes, `SIGHUP` on the tui_gateway; here every ~20–60 min).
- On shutdown, `tui_gateway` marks all held sessions `end_reason='tui_shutdown'`.
- `display.tui_auto_resume_recent` defaults to `false`, so the next launch calls `newSession()` and the user lands in an empty conversation. From the user's perspective the previous conversation "disappeared", though every message is present in `state.db` (verified message-by-message against the logs).
- `session.resume` does call `reopen_session()` and restores the full transcript, so the data is always recoverable — the problem is purely that nothing resumes it automatically and the session list/navigation is the only way back.

## Symptom 3 — multiple windows race the same session

With `tui_auto_resume_recent` enabled and several desktop windows open, every window auto-resumes the same most-recent session; `session.activate`/`close` churn between windows caused connection flapping (9-second connect/disconnect cycles) and intermittent `session.resume` failures.

## Workaround (verified)

```bash
hermes config set display.tui_auto_resume_recent true
```

plus: use a single desktop window, and recover any ended session via `session.resume` (it reopens ended sessions) or the dashboard SESSIONS page.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `run_agent`/`hermes_state`, on `SessionCompressionInProgressError`, wait for the lock (bounded, e.g. up to the lock TTL) and retry the append instead of aborting the turn.
2. Make the "session storage could not be written" message distinguish disk-full from compression-lock contention.
3. Consider defaulting `display.tui_auto_resume_recent` to `true` for the desktop surface (or auto-reopening the last active session after an abnormal disconnect), and/or not marking sessions `tui_shutdown` when the disconnect was abnormal.

## Environment

- Hermes 0.20.0 (dev), desktop app (embedded TUI) → dashboard web server → tui_gateway; gateway in Docker, client over LAN.
- `state.db` (SQLite, WAL), `sessions/` JSONL storage.

items.title: Cron + background delegate_task: shared SessionDB use-after-close silently drops child transcripts; completions unroutable (session_key=<cli>); missing Discord send/edit-message tool
