items.title: [Bug]: CLI deadlocks and terminal UI corrupts when provider stream stalls — regression in 2026.8.3 retry/relay machinery

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Bug Description

After updating to 2026.8.3 (commit b3aa561f, ~223 commits past the previous release), the interactive CLI deadlocks and the terminal UI corrupts when the provider stream stalls mid-response. The provider (opencode-go) returned an empty stream (HTTP 200, zero chunks, no finish_reason). Instead of recovering like the previous version did, the CLI enters a state where:

- The main thread pegs at ~70-93% CPU (state R, spinning)
- The process writes hundreds of escape-sequence writes per second to the PTY (~400-700/sec measured), causing a flickering input bar
- SIGTERM does NOT unwind it (the graceful-exit handler is stuck in the same broken state). Only SIGKILL works
- The session is lost (must be killed)

This happened 3+ times in one evening, always following a provider stream stall. The SAME config and SAME provider on the previous build (d92a28dd) ran all day without a single occurrence, and reverting to d92a28dd fixed it completely. Config is not a factor: config version 33, `hermes config check` passes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes` (interactive CLI) in a terminal (reproduced in kitty on Wayland)
2. Send a message that triggers a provider stream stall — e.g. opencode-go going silent mid-response (logged as `EmptyStreamError: Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason`, HTTP 200, zero chunks). Any provider that intermittently stalls should trigger it; opencode-go was flaky that evening.
3. The CLI logs stream-retry attempts ("retry 2/3"), then "Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (22.6s elapsed)"
4. The UI corrupts: input bar flickers, main thread pegs CPU, terminal flooded with escape sequences
5. Ctrl+C / SIGTERM cannot recover it; the process must be SIGKILLed

## Expected Behavior

A provider stream stall should be retried or surfaced as an error gracefully (as it was on d92a28dd), with the CLI UI intact and the session recoverable.

## Actual Behavior

Deadlock + UI corruption: ~70-93% CPU on the main thread, ~400-700 escape-sequence writes/sec to the PTY, flickering input bar, SIGTERM ineffective, session lost.

## Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Agent Core (conversation loop)

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

[PENDING — will run `hermes debug share` and add links if requested]

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux (kernel 7.1.6-arch1-1), Wayland/Hyprland
- Terminal: kitty
- Python Version: 3.11.15 (venv)
- Hermes Version: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), broken commit b3aa561f
- Provider: opencode-go (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, chat_completions), model deepseek-v4-flash
- Config version: 33 (validated)

## Additional Logs / Evidence

- `EmptyStreamError: Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason` (HTTP 200, zero chunks)
- Stream retry attempts logged ("retry 2/3") before the deadlock
- `Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (22.6s elapsed)`
- `relay session scope close failed: scope handle is not at the top of the stack`
- `process_loop unhandled error: [Errno 5] Input/output error`
- Process telemetry at deadlock: ~1.5M read syscalls / ~575K write syscalls, +1,600+ write syscalls per 4s window to the PTY, main thread in R state

## Root Cause Analysis

The 2026.8.3 update (b3aa561f) substantially rewrote the stream/retry/relay paths: `agent/tool_executor.py` (+367 lines), `run_agent.py` (+262), `agent/transports/chat_completions.py`, `agent/transports/codex.py` (+238), plus new relay machinery. EmptyStreamError handling existed BEFORE this update (`agent/errors.py`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — the `_call()` retry loop treats it as retryable) and recovered cleanly on d92a28dd. Post-update, a stalled stream deadlocks instead of recovering: the relay session close fails, the process loop hits EIO, and then a renderer loop floods the terminal indefinitely. I could not pin the exact line (no live stack access at the time), but the regression is squarely in this rewritten machinery. Note also #65631 (empty-stream misclassification) and #81025 (stream drops mid-tool-call) which look like related expressions of the same area.

## Related Issues

- #81025 — Anthropic mid-tool-call drop after preamble text: no in-place stream retry (filed same day, same area)
- #18019 — Stream stalled mid tool-call (marked duplicate)
- #65631 — Provider error chunk misclassified as "empty stream" and retried forever
- #51448 — "empty stream, no finish_reason" (desktop/Windows variant)

## Workaround

Pin to the previous build: `git checkout d92a28dd` (or run a stable branch). This is a hard stop for anyone affected — the only recovery is SIGKILL.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

Re-verify the stream-stall path in the rewritten retry/relay code: on EmptyStreamError / silent stream, the retry loop must terminate cleanly (bounded retries then a surfaced error), the relay session scope must close without corrupting the process loop, and the terminal renderer must never enter an unbounded redraw loop.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

No (I'm not a contributor), but happy to provide more logs/telemetry or test candidate fixes.

items.title: dashboard fd leak: OSError [Errno 24] Too many open files after several days on macOS

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
# Dashboard fd leak: `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files` after several days

## Summary

Long-running `hermes dashboard` (LaunchAgent-managed, macOS) exhausts its
file descriptor soft limit and starts throwing `OSError: [Errno 24] Too
many open files` from any request handler that calls `os.listdir` /
`open`. The dashboard process stays alive (uvicorn swallows the exception
inside starlette middleware), but every API request that touches
`/Users/eight/.hermes/profiles`, `/skills`, or `cron/jobs.json` silently
fails. Remote clients (Hermes Desktop on another Mac) see "connection
timed out" and can't reach the dashboard.

## Environment

- macOS Tahoe 26.4.1, `launchctl limit maxfiles = 256` (soft) /
  `unlimited` (hard)
- Hermes `0.19.1` (current main: `0044876a1`)
- Dashboard started via `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.dashboard.plist`
  as `--no-open --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119`
- `state.db` file is 858 MB after ~3 months uptime

## Reproduction

1. Install Hermes, start `dashboard --host 0.0.0.0` via launchd
2. Let it run for several days while clients hit `/api/profiles`,
   `/api/skills`, `/api/cron` regularly
3. `lsof -p $(lsof -nP -iTCP:9119 -sTCP:LISTEN | awk 'NR==2{print $2}') | wc -l`
   shows fd count climbing past 256
4. First symptom: `/Users/eight/.hermes/logs/dashboard.error.log` starts
   showing:

   ```
   OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '/Users/eight/.hermes/profiles'
   OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '/Users/eight/.hermes/skills'
   OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '/Users/eight/.hermes/cron/jobs.json'
   ```

   The full traceback is rooted at
   `hermes_cli/web_routers/profiles.py:344 list_profiles_endpoint` calling
   `_fallback_profile_dicts` → `profiles_mod._get_profiles_root().iterdir()`
   → `os.listdir()`.

5. From another Mac: `curl http://<host>:9119/api/health` returns nothing
   (uvicorn swallows the exception, client times out). Dashboard process
   still listens but every endpoint that hits a `Path.iterdir()` blows up.

## Diagnosis (from a real case)

- macOS default `maxfiles` soft limit is 256. The Hermes LaunchAgent plist
  does **not** raise `ulimit -n`, so the dashboard inherits 256.
- `d10d3d7b4 fix(gateway,tools,agent): close leaked SQLite connections in
  delivery, delegation, and verification ledgers` already fixed a related
  leak in three ledgers by introducing `_transaction()` (close on exit)
  vs `with _connect()` (sqlite3 context manager only commits/rolls back —
  does not close the connection).
- That fix does **not** cover the dashboard's request paths. `web_server.py`
  constructs `SessionDB(db_path=Path(home) / "state.db")` from many
  endpoints; the connections appear to outlive each request under load.
  `/api/profiles` and `/api/skills` are the visible hot paths.
- `6d879d486 fix(dashboard): close PTY WebSocket on child EOF to stop FD
  leak` already addressed one specific dashboard leak (PTY master fd), but
  the general ledger/dashboard connection lifecycle still leaks.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Dashboard should raise `ulimit -n` on startup** before binding uvicorn.
   macOS default 256 is too tight for any process that opens `state.db` +
   `state.db-wal` + `state.db-shm` per connection across many threads.
   This is the cheapest stopgap and prevents `OSError 24` from masking the
   underlying bug.
2. **Audit every `SessionDB(...)` construction in `hermes_cli/web_server.py`
   and `hermes_cli/web_routers/`** — make sure each instance is either
   closed explicitly or used through a single shared connection (the
   `app.state` singleton pattern, like `app.state.sdb`).
3. **Adopt the `_transaction()` helper for any path that opens a fresh
   connection** (same shape as the fix in `d10d3d7b4`).

## Workaround applied locally

Until this is fixed upstream, the user has applied:

- A: Wrapped the dashboard LaunchAgent `ProgramArguments` in `/bin/sh -c
  'ulimit -n 65536; exec ...'` so the process inherits 65536 instead of
  256. File: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.dashboard.plist`
- B: Added a 4-hourly cron watchdog that runs `lsof -p <pid> | wc -l`,
  comparing to a 200-fd threshold; if exceeded it restarts via
  `launchctl kickstart -k`. File:
  `/Users/eight/.hermes/scripts/dashboard-fd-watchdog.sh`

These workarounds are noise-tolerant (the watchdog is silent when
healthy) but they restart the dashboard every few days, which is still
disruptive for live clients.

## Impact

- Severity: **medium** — only affects long-running dashboard installs
  on macOS with default soft fd limit. Linux systemd services usually
  inherit 1024+ so the symptom is rare there.
- Reproducible: yes, in production within 2-7 days depending on traffic.
- Workaround: exists (this issue).

## Related commits / issues

- `d10d3d7b4 fix(gateway,tools,agent): close leaked SQLite connections`
  — sibling fix for three ledgers.
- `a266155cc fix(cli): untrack sqlite connections only after close
  succeeds`
- `6d879d486 fix(dashboard): close PTY WebSocket on child EOF to stop FD
  leak (#54028)`
- `113d9f63b fix: Windows guard, dedup recovery, profile-safe paths,
  clear SO_RCVTIMEO`
- PR #54028 (PTY fd leak)
- Issue #69678 (SQLite FD leak infographic)

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway balloons to ~60GB RSS every ~2h, OOM-freezes whole machine — regression in v2026.8.3 (0.20.0)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

The gateway process (`hermes-gateway.service`) grows from ~150 MB to **54–64 GB RSS in ~2-hour cycles**, exhausting all 62 GB RAM (only 2 GB swap), which freezes the whole desktop and forces a reboot. From the user's perspective it looked like a kernel panic, but there is no actual panic — it is OOM exhaustion.

**This is a regression introduced in `v2026.8.3` (0.20.0).** Rolling back to `v2026.7.30` (0.19.1) completely resolves it. The machine is a stock Zorin OS 18 Pro (Ubuntu 24.04 base) desktop; the regression reproduced on kernels 6.17 and 6.8, so it is not kernel/OS related.

No Python traceback is produced — the process is killed by OOM while the event loop is still nominally running.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Update to `v2026.8.3` (0.20.0).
2. Start the gateway: `hermes gateway run` (or the systemd user unit `hermes-gateway.service`).
3. Wait ~2 hours.

Details:
- The gateway idles at ~150 MB RSS; its own housekeeping trims RSS every 60 s (`mem_trim` lines in `agent.log`) and stays stable for the first ~1 h of each cycle.
- In the last ~30–60 min of each cycle RSS climbs rapidly to 54–64 GB → OOM kill → system freeze.
- Deaths repeat every ~2 h 05 m (e.g. 02:09, 04:18, 06:27, 08:33, 10:09 UTC).
- The watchdog logs `Gateway event loop missed 3 consecutive liveness probes; dumping all thread stacks and exiting with code 75` and systemd restarts the unit (`Restart=always`).

Lifecycle/OOM records (from `agent.log` / gateway state):

```
suspected_oom=True
last_mem={'rss_kib': 54616064, 'mem_total_kib': 65772392, 'mem_available_kib': 71292, 'swap_used_kib': 2097048}
```

Example: `pid=124247` started 05:51 UTC, last heartbeat 07:50 UTC, `rss_kib=54616064` at death.

### Expected Behavior

Gateway memory should stay bounded at the ~150 MB the housekeeping trims to, indefinitely.

### Actual Behavior

RSS balloons to 54–64 GB and the process is OOM-killed every ~2 h; during the climb the entire machine becomes unresponsive (all RAM consumed), requiring a hard reboot.

### Affected Component

- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) — using Slack

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- Slack

### Debug Report

I have rolled back to `v2026.7.30` (0.19.1), so the current logs are from the working release and `hermes debug share` would upload 0.19.1 data rather than the failing build. I can share the 0.20.0-era logs (`agent.log`, `gateway-exit-diag.log`) on request. Note: I avoided `hermes debug share` to avoid uploading config/secrets.

### Operating System

Zorin OS 18 Pro (Ubuntu 24.04 base), kernel 6.8.0-137-generic (also reproduced on 6.17.0-40)

### Python Version

3.11.15 (venv)

### Hermes Version

0.20.0 (regressed) → 0.19.1 (rolled back, working)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

No traceback; OOM kills. Two observations that may help pinpoint the culprit:

1. **A periodic task runs roughly every 2 h** and is the prime suspect. `agent.log` logs a `snapshot created` approximately every 2 h (e.g. 02:44:54Z, 04:44:21Z, 06:50:26Z, 08:51:30Z UTC), which lines up with the ~2 h death cycle. This is **inconsistent** with `curator.interval_hours: 168` (weekly) in `config.yaml` — something else is scheduling snapshots every ~2 h.
2. **The gateway rewrites its own systemd unit file on every start** ("Updated gateway user service definition to match the current Hermes install"), which wipes any user-added `MemoryMax`/`MemoryHigh` lines. A systemd drop-in works, but consider using a config option or `container_memory`-style setting instead of rewriting the unit.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Not fully identified. The main loop stays at ~154 MB via 60-second `mem_trim` housekeeping, so the balloon must originate in a periodic background task that loads a large amount of data into memory (the 2-hour snapshot producer is the leading candidate). The mismatch between the observed ~2 h snapshot cadence and the configured 168 h curator interval suggests a scheduler regression between 0.19.1 and 0.20.0.

Workaround that keeps the desktop usable: set `MemoryMax=8G`/`MemoryHigh=6G` via a systemd **drop-in** (`hermes-gateway.service.d/`) so only the gateway is OOM-killed and restarts after 5 s instead of freezing the whole machine.

items.title: [Bug]: _canonicalize_api_tool_calls` mutates stored history on the repair path (contradicting its own docstring); `{}`-substituted tool calls leave sessions permanently stuck in reasoning-only responses

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Issue — Unrepairable tool_call arguments are replaced with `{}` **and written through to persisted history**, leaving the session unable to answer

### Summary

When a tool call's `arguments` JSON cannot be repaired, Hermes substitutes an
empty object and continues. Two things then go wrong:

**1. The substitution is written through to the persisted transcript.**
`_canonicalize_api_tool_calls` (`agent/conversation_loop.py:793-825`) documents
itself as non-destructive:

```python
# conversation_loop.py:796-797
# Rewrites each message's ``tool_calls`` in place (copy-on-write for the
# tool-call dicts it canonicalizes; the persisted history is untouched).
```

The success path honours that — it rebinds a **copy**:

```python
# conversation_loop.py:811-818
try:
    tc = {**tc, "function": {
        **tc["function"],
        "arguments": _canonicalize_tool_call_arguments(tc["function"]["arguments"]),
    }}
```

The failure path does **not** — it assigns into the original dict:

```python
# conversation_loop.py:819-822
except Exception:
    tc["function"]["arguments"] = _repair_tool_call_arguments(   # ← mutates the ORIGINAL
        tc["function"]["arguments"],
        tc["function"].get("name", "?"),
    )
```

So exactly in the case where the value is degraded to `"{}"`
(`agent/message_sanitization.py:280`), it is persisted — the caller's
`api_messages` entries share the tool-call dicts with stored history. The
docstring's guarantee holds only while nothing goes wrong.

**2. The resulting transcript is not recoverable in-session.** The turn is left
in history as an assistant message carrying a tool call with `{}` arguments,
followed by a tool result that is necessarily an error (`{}` never satisfies a
tool schema). From that point the model returns reasoning-only / near-empty
completions on every subsequent turn, and the session never produces a visible
answer again. `repair_empty_non_final_messages`
(`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:3169-3235`) fires on every following request —
by design it only repairs the wire copy (`:3193` "stored conversation history is
never mutated"), so it re-heals the same turn forever instead of once.

Observed tail, every time:

```
WARNING agent.message_sanitization: Unrepairable tool_call arguments for <tool>
        — replaced with empty object (was: …)
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: Empty response (no content or reasoning) — retry 1/3 … 3/3
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: Reasoning-only response (no visible content) after
        exhausting retries and fallback. Reasoning: [response interrupted]<|im_end|>
INFO    agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=empty_response_exhausted
```

Completion sizes in the stuck state are `out=1`, `4`, `5`, `8`, `12` tokens —
the model emits little more than the stop token, while input stays at ~23K
tokens (well inside a 256K window).

### Why this is not one bug in one tool

The `{}` substitution is reached from unrelated directions. All four incidents
below are the same code path with different upstream causes:

| Date | Tool | What made the arguments unparsable | Transport | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-22 16:55 | `web_search` | tool-parser artifact: `{"limit": "<arg_key>query…` | — | recovered |
| 2026-08-04 21:02 / 21:18 | `write_file` | stream died mid-arguments (auth/transport drop) | desktop app | **stuck** |
| 2026-08-06 17:44 | `write_file` | stream died mid-arguments | desktop app | recovered |
| 2026-08-07 21:46 | `memory` | model emitted `{"action": …}` instead of the required `{"operations": [ … ]}` | **Telegram** | **stuck** |

Two different platforms, three different tools, and both a transport cause and
a pure model-output cause. Whether a session recovers or dies appears to be
chance: 2026-08-06 had the same trigger as 2026-08-04 and came back on the next
API call.

### Environment

* Hermes Agent **v0.20.0** (`2026.8.3`), Docker, split deployment: gateway
  (Telegram) + `hermes serve` (desktop backend), shared `HERMES_HOME`
  (`/opt/data`).
* Model: `Qwen3.6-27B-AEON-…-MTP` via vLLM (`max_model_len=256000`,
  `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`) behind LiteLLM.
* Affected sessions: `20260804_204029_be0e9d` (desktop),
  `20260807_110305_85e2a27f` (telegram).

### Steps to Reproduce

What we could NOT establish. Stated explicitly so nobody over-reads this report:

* **No deterministic reproduction of the stuck state.** Replaying the degenerate
  transcript shape (assistant turn with empty content + `{}` arguments +
  error tool result) against the same model did *not* reproduce the `out=1`
  signature — the model instead consumed the whole completion budget in
  reasoning. A control run with only the bare user message behaved identically,
  so that test isolates nothing and is not evidence.
* Consequently we cannot claim which of the suggested fixes actually stops the
  stuck state. Fix 1 is justified on its own terms (the code contradicts its
  docstring); fixes 2–4 are reasoned from the logs, not verified.
* Why the model answers with a single stop token in the poisoned state is
  **unknown**. Context pressure is ruled out (~23K of 256K).

### Expected Behavior

* Session does not get permanently stuck in reasoning-only responses

### Actual Behavior

Impact :

* A single unparsable tool call can end a conversation permanently. The user
  sees only "The model produced only internal reasoning and no final answer",
  and every further message in that session reproduces it.
* Because the degraded value is persisted, restarting the gateway does not
  help; the session has to be abandoned.
* Weak/open models are disproportionately affected — they are both likelier to
  emit malformed tool arguments and likelier to respond to the degenerate turn
  with an immediate stop token. Observed with a 27B-class local model behind
  LiteLLM/vLLM.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory), Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
None
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. **Honour the documented contract on the failure path** — make the `except`
   branch copy-on-write like the success branch, so a `{}` substitution never
   reaches stored history:
   ```python
   except Exception:
       tc = {**tc, "function": {
           **tc["function"],
           "arguments": _repair_tool_call_arguments(
               tc["function"]["arguments"], tc["function"].get("name", "?")),
       }}
   ```
   One-line-shaped change, and it makes the existing docstring true.
2. **Do not send a tool call that has no arguments left.** Rather than emitting
   `{}` and letting the tool reject it, drop the tool call from the assistant
   turn and synthesise a tool result explaining that the call was malformed and
   should be re-emitted. `close_interrupted_tool_sequence`
   (`agent/message_sanitization.py:283`) already establishes this pattern —
   an explicit placeholder turn rather than a degenerate one.
3. **Repair persisted history once, not the wire copy forever.** If
   `repair_empty_non_final_messages` has to heal the same turn on every request,
   the stored transcript is broken and should be repaired in place (or the
   session flagged), instead of masking it per-call.
4. **Tolerate the single-operation form in the `memory` tool** (or state the
   required shape in the tool description). The model failed the
   `{"operations": [...]}` schema three times in a row before giving up; the
   error text `"operations must be a list of {action, content?, old_text?}
   objects."` is only emitted after the call already failed.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Completed-turn assistant replies are never persisted to state.db when the session disconnects/reaps — lost after Desktop restart (v0.20.0, remote serve over Tailscale / direct IP)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

On a remote Hermes backend (Docker, `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` = **v0.20.0**) accessed by the Hermes Desktop client over a Tailscale / direct-IP path (and a Cloudflare tunnel domain), an assistant reply that **completes and is visible in the Desktop UI** is **missing from `state.db`** after the session ends / the client disconnects / the Desktop app is restarted.

The symptom is **not cosmetic** — re-hydrating the session (switching conversations, or restarting the Desktop app, both of which re-fetch from the backend store) does **not** recover the reply, because the backend store genuinely lacks the assistant rows.

This is distinct from:
- **#79635** — same `ws_orphan_reap` mechanism, but the reporter states `state.db` is intact and clicking away/back self-heals (cosmetic). Our case is the genuine-loss variant.
- **#79050** — renderer hydrate-overwrite of a completed turn, recoverable by restarting Hermes. Different: in our case the data is never in the store at all.
- **#69455 / #79455** — chat history collapses to current turn (renderer-only). Different root cause.

## Environment

- Hermes **v0.20.0** (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`)
- Backend: Docker container, dashboard on `:9119` (published `:2053`)
- Access paths: Hermes Desktop connects to the backend over a **non-loopback** path — both a **Tailscale / direct-IP** address and a **Cloudflare tunnel domain** (i.e. not `127.0.0.1`). Specific endpoints redacted for privacy.
- Client: Hermes Desktop (Electron) on Windows 11
- Backend host: Linux (remote VPS)

## Observed behavior

1. User sends a message; the turn **completes** and the assistant reply is **shown in the Desktop UI**.
2. The conversation ends / the client goes idle / the WebSocket disconnects and the session is reaped (`ws_orphan_reap`).
3. Later, **switching conversations OR restarting the Desktop app** shows the assistant reply **gone**.
4. Direct inspection of `state.db` (`/opt/data/.hermes/state.db`, `messages` table) for the affected sessions shows **0 assistant rows** — only the user messages are present.

Because a Desktop restart re-fetches from the backend store, the reply being absent after restart proves the backend `state.db` **never contained it** — a genuine persistence gap, not a renderer/hydrate issue.

Example sessions (verified via `sqlite3`/`SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=... GROUP BY role`):
- `20260807_120409_c27ce7` → 33 `user` rows, **0 assistant**
- `20260808_084649_3b07e7` → 0 assistant

## Root cause (analysis)

- The assistant reply is delivered to the UI via the **interim / streaming display path** (`_emit_interim_assistant_message` in `run_agent.py`), which by design **updates the UI only and does NOT persist** to `state.db`.
- The only durable write of a pure-text assistant turn happens at **turn end** (`conversation_loop.py:1913`, a single `messages.append({"role":"assistant", ...})`), flushed by `_finalize_session` / `_flush_messages_to_session_db`.
- If the WebSocket disconnects and the session is reaped (`ws_orphan_reap`, gated by `HERMES_TUI_WS_ORPHAN_REAP_GRACE_S`, default 20s) **around the moment the turn completes**, the finalize/flush can race the reap: the session is finalized with a stale `_session_messages` snapshot (or the interim buffer is discarded) and the assistant row is never durably committed.
- This is made far more likely by the **hardcoded `ws_ping_timeout=20.0`** on non-loopback binds (see #79635) for remote/Tailscale paths, which causes frequent `1006` closures → `ws_orphan_reap`. Per #79635 there is currently **no config/env override** for the ping timeout.

Note: the `_AutoPersistList` mechanism (`per_message_persist.py`) only flushes on `append()`; the streaming interim path updates in place / via UI only, so it does not capture the in-flight reply. This matches the documented behavior that interim messages are display-only.

## Related

- #79635 — same `ws_orphan_reap`, but cosmetic (state.db intact). Ours is the genuine-loss variant.
- #79050 — renderer hydrate-overwrite of a completed turn (recoverable by restart). Different: ours is not in the store.
- #79455 — chat history collapses to current turn (renderer). Different root cause.
- #69940 — Desktop WS disconnects → orphan reap → chats lost on close/reopen (closest sibling: genuine loss).
- #54523 — async routes block the asyncio loop over Tailscale, starving the WS (independent cause of the `1006` drops that trigger the reap).

## Suggested fix

1. **Persist streaming assistant text incrementally (primary):** maintain an in-progress assistant message in `_session_messages` as deltas arrive, and explicitly flush it to `state.db` during streaming (not only at turn end), so a disconnect/reap cannot lose already-produced text. Reuse the existing `_flush_messages_to_session_db` + `_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER` dedup; on turn finalize, replace the in-progress row with the full reply.
2. **Expose `ws_ping_interval` / `ws_ping_timeout`** in `config.yaml`/env (per #79635) and relax the non-loopback default from 20s to ~60s, reducing the frequency of `1006`→reap events that trigger the race.
3. **Add a short reconnect grace before reaping** a detached session (per #79635 option 3), so transient disconnects self-heal without dropping in-flight state.

## Reproduction

1. Point Hermes Desktop at a remote backend over Tailscale / direct IP (non-loopback).
2. Start a conversation; let the assistant produce a multi-paragraph reply (pure text, no tool calls).
3. Immediately after the reply completes, disconnect the client (or let it idle until the WS drops / the session is reaped), then restart the Desktop app (or switch away and back).
4. Inspect `state.db` `messages` for that session — the assistant row is absent / the reply is gone in the UI.

## Suggested labels

`bug`, `desktop`, `comp/gateway` (session dispatch / delivery), `sweeper:risk-session-state`, `sweeper:risk-message-delivery`

items.title: [Bug]: Stalled event loop makes `hermes update` hang — updater waits 180s for a gateway that cannot shut down

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

A stalled gateway event loop does not only break chat — **it also makes `hermes update` hang indefinitely**. The updater asks the gateway to shut down and waits for it; a gateway whose event loop is blocked never processes the shutdown, so the updater waits, warns after 180 s, and then deadlocks.

This gives the event-loop stall a second, much more visible failure mode than the one described in #72707: **the user cannot update their way out of it**, because the update itself is a victim of the stall.

Stopping the services *before* updating turns a reproducible hang into a clean 40-second run. That is a usable workaround today and, I think, a hint at the right fix.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**, git checkout current as of 2026-08-08
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.11, launchd-managed `ai.hermes.gateway` + `ai.hermes.dashboard`
- Local inference provider (OpenAI-compatible, on `127.0.0.1`)
- Large state: `state.db` 391 MB, 783 sessions, ~40 000 messages

## Symptom

`hermes update` — both from the desktop app and from a terminal — stops after:

```
→ Syncing bundled skills...
  ~ 2 user-modified (kept)
  ✓ Skills are up to date
```

…and never returns. Observed twice from the desktop app and once from a terminal. The process sits at **0.0 % CPU**, has **no child processes**, and its log file stops growing. In one case it sat there for 7 min 48 s before being killed manually; in another, ~45 minutes.

A second `hermes update` is correctly refused (the lock works):

```
✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID …, started 6m 1s ago).
```

So a hung update **blocks every subsequent update attempt** until the stale process is killed by hand.

## Evidence

**1. The updater says it out loud** (this line is easy to miss — it scrolls past mid-run, and the run *appears* to finish afterwards):

```
⚠ Gateway PID 13820 still running after 180.0s — restart may fail
```

**2. Thread stack of the hung updater** (`sample <pid>`): both threads parked in a lock wait, nothing running.

```
pythread_wrapper → thread_run → method_vectorcall → _PyFunction_Vectorcall
  → PyThread_acquire_lock_timed
    → _pthread_cond_wait
      → __psynch_cvwait
```

No open sockets, no child processes — not a network stall, a lock wait.

**3. Counter-proof.** Same machine, same checkout, minutes apart:

| Gateway state during `hermes update` | Result |
|---|---|
| running (event loop stalled) | hangs indefinitely, `⚠ … still running after 180.0s` |
| stopped beforehand | **completes in 40 s, zero warnings** |

## What stalls the loop here

In this installation the trigger is **session compression**. One session had crossed `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit` (416 messages vs. a limit of 400), so *every* inbound message started a compression pass:

```
Session hygiene: 416 messages, ~194,010 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing
```

…which blocks the loop, and ~2 minutes later:

```
CRITICAL gateway.shutdown_watchdog: Gateway event loop missed 3 consecutive liveness probes;
dumping all thread stacks and exiting with code …
```

Timeline was reproducible to the second: inbound message → compression → dead gateway ~2 min later, then auto-resume replays the same session on boot and the cycle repeats. 15 kills in one morning.

Relevant: `web_server.py` already moves work off the loop via `asyncio.to_thread` / `run_in_executor` (with a telling comment that `run_in_executor` *still* froze the loop for 15–22 s). But the **gateway-side session compression is not offloaded** — in `gateway/` only `channel_directory.py` uses `asyncio.to_thread`. So the class of bug in #72707 is partially addressed for websockets and still open on the compression path.

## Two smaller findings that make it worse

**a) `compression.timeout` and the loop watchdog are tuned against each other.**

- `models.compression.timeout` default here: **180 s**
- Loop watchdog: `DEFAULT_LOOP_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_S = 30`, `MAX_STRIKES = 3` → kill at **~90 s**

Compression is therefore *allowed* twice as long as the process is *permitted to live*. It can never finish; it can only get the gateway killed. Any value of `compression.timeout` above ~80 s is unreachable by construction.

**b) `restart_loop_guard` cannot trip on a slow loop.**

It trips at `DEFAULT_MAX_RESTARTS = 3` within `DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS = 60`. The crash cycle here was ~150 s (compression → 90 s watchdog → restart → auto-resume). So the counter never exceeded 1 and `gateway/restart_loop.json` kept a single timestamp:

```json
{"boots": [1786180127.268378]}
```

The circuit breaker built for exactly this scenario is dimensioned for fast respawn loops (~10 s) and silently misses slow ones.

## Reproduction

1. Let a session grow past `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit`.
2. Send a message to that session → compression starts → gateway is killed ~90 s later.
3. While that is happening, run `hermes update` → it warns after 180 s and hangs.
4. Kill the updater, stop gateway + dashboard, run `hermes update` again → completes in seconds.

## Workaround

Stop the services first, update, then bring them back:

```bash
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/ai.hermes.gateway
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/ai.hermes.dashboard
hermes update
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.dashboard.plist
```

To keep the underlying stall from triggering at all, keep sessions below `hygiene_hard_message_limit`, and set `models.compression.timeout` **below** the watchdog window (~75 s) so compression aborts instead of getting the process killed — `compression.abort_on_summary_failure: false` then lets the gateway carry on uncompressed rather than dying.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Bound the updater's wait and escalate.** After the existing 180 s warning, force-terminate the gateway rather than waiting on a process that is provably not scheduling. Today the warning is printed and the updater still hangs.
2. **Offload session compression** off the event loop (`asyncio.to_thread`), same treatment `web_server.py` already got.
3. **Derive `compression.timeout` from the watchdog budget** (or validate at startup and warn), so it cannot exceed the time the process is allowed to live.
4. **Make `restart_loop_guard` time-window aware** — a window of 60 s cannot see a 150 s crash cycle. Counting boots-with-pending-resume over a longer window (or counting consecutive occurrences regardless of spacing) would have broken this loop automatically.
5. **Stale-lock detection for the update lock.** A hung updater blocks all further updates; a liveness check on the lock holder (0 % CPU, no children, no log growth for N minutes) would let the next run take over.

Related: #72707 (event loop stall / GIL), #41737 and #37775 (desktop update freezes).

Happy to provide more logs or test a patch — this installation reproduces it readily.

items.title: Bug: read_file misclassifies valid UTF-8 text as binary when the 1000-byte sample cut lands mid-multibyte-character

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
# Bug: read_file misclassifies valid UTF-8 text as binary when the 1000-byte sample cut lands mid-multibyte-character

**Version**: Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
**Platform**: Linux

## Summary

`read_file` reports `Binary file - cannot display as text` for **valid UTF-8 text files** (Chinese markdown docs, e.g. READMEs) whenever the 1000-byte sampling cut happens to split a multi-byte UTF-8 character. The file itself is fine: `file` says `Unicode text, UTF-8 text`, `cat`/`sed` read it normally, and the `patch` tool edits it fine. Only `read_file` misclassifies it — deterministically (same file, same cut position → always binary).

## Root cause

In `tools/file_operations.py`, `read_file` samples the first 1000 **bytes** via shell:

```python
sample_cmd = f"head -c 1000 {self._escape_shell_arg(path)} 2>/dev/null"
sample_result = self._exec(sample_cmd)
sample_output = _strip_terminal_fence_leaks(sample_result.stdout)
```

The terminal env decodes stdout with `errors="replace"`, so if byte 1000 lands inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character (e.g. a CJK char which is 3 bytes), `head`'s output ends with a half-decoded character → `U+FFFD` replacement char.

Then `_is_likely_binary` (line ~885) treats U+FFFD as proof of binary content:

```python
if "\ufffd" in content_sample[:1000]:
    return True
```

So a perfectly valid UTF-8 text file whose 1000th byte is mid-character is classified as binary. For Chinese-heavy documents, byte 1000 has roughly a 2/3 chance of falling inside a 3-byte CJK character, so this triggers constantly for CJK docs while almost never for ASCII files.

## Repro

```bash
# Create a valid UTF-8 file whose 1000th byte is inside a CJK char:
python3 -c "
import pathlib
pathlib.Path('/tmp/repro.md').write_bytes(
    ('a中' * 256).encode('utf-8') + b'a' + b'\n')  # 1025 bytes, byte 1000 is 0xB8 (middle of 中)
"
file /tmp/repro.md          # → Unicode text, UTF-8 text
cat /tmp/repro.md           # → prints fine
```

Then `read_file('/tmp/repro.md')` → `Binary file - cannot display as text` (is_binary=true).

## Evidence

Byte-level analysis of the 1000-byte cut point vs `read_file` outcome:

| file | size | byte 1000 | decodes? | read_file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ascii 3690B | 3690 | 0x61 | yes | ✅ text |
| CJK 662B | 662 | n/a (<1000, no cut) | yes | ✅ text |
| CJK 1016B | 1016 | 0x0A (newline) | yes | ✅ text |
| CJK 1542B | 1542 | 0xBB (mid-char) | **no** | ❌ binary |
| CJK 4353B | 4353 | 0xBB (mid-char) | **no** | ❌ binary |

Also: splitting the 1542B file into two files of 662B + 881B (both < 1000B, no cut) → both read fine; the same lines concatenated → binary again. Reversing line order doesn't help; removing blank lines shifts byte 1000 to a character boundary → file reads fine again. All consistent with the byte-1000 cut theory.

## Suggested fix

Sample on a **character boundary** instead of a raw byte cut, e.g.:

```python
sample_cmd = f"head -c 1001 {self._escape_shell_arg(path)} 2>/dev/null"  # then drop the last char
```

or better, decode with `errors="ignore"` before the U+FFFD check, or read the sample with `head -c 1000` and then **strip a trailing partial character** (e.g. use `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 sed -n '1p'`-style line-based sampling, or `head -c 1000 | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 -c`).

Minimal fix: in `_is_likely_binary`, only treat U+FFFD as binary when the *file itself* (not the truncated sample) contains U+FFFD — e.g. check `sample_output` for U+FFFD *not in the final 3 bytes* (the only place a truncation-induced U+FFFD can appear), or simply skip the U+FFFD heuristic when the sample length is exactly the truncation length and the raw tail bytes show a partial UTF-8 sequence.

## Workaround (for users)

Read such files with `terminal` (`cat`, `sed`) or the `patch` tool instead of `read_file` — both handle UTF-8 correctly.

items.body:
# Bug: read_file flags all CJK/UTF-8 text files as binary when `head -c 1000` cuts a multibyte char

## Summary

`read_file` returns `is_binary=True` ("Binary file - cannot display as text") for **every** text file whose first 1000 bytes contain a multibyte UTF-8 character (i.e. all Chinese/Japanese/Korean text, most accented Latin text). The file is then unreadable via the tool. Severity: high for CJK users — effectively every `.md`/`.txt`/source file with Chinese content fails to read.

## Root cause

`tools/file_operations.py` → `read_file()`:

1. Samples the file with `head -c 1000` (line 1168).
2. The terminal env decodes stdout with `errors="replace"` (documented in `_is_likely_binary`).
3. `_is_likely_binary()` then does:
   ```python
   if "\ufffd" in content_sample[:1000]:
       return True
   ```

For any UTF-8 file with multibyte characters, byte index 999 lands mid-character roughly 2/3 of the time (CJK chars are 3 bytes). The truncated tail decodes to a single U+FFFD replacement char — a *sampling artifact*, not real corruption — and the check above immediately flags the whole file as binary.

## Repro

```bash
printf '中文测试文本' > /tmp/cjk.txt   # 3-byte chars; head -c 1000 cuts mid-char
```
- `read_file("/tmp/cjk.txt")` → `is_binary=True, error="Binary file - cannot display as text."`
- A pure-ASCII file of any length → reads fine.

Observed on `三重特攻01.md` (a 4.4 KB Chinese screenplay) and `SKILL.md` of the humanizer-zh skill (18.9 KB) — both flagged binary.

## Fix (proposed, minimal)

A single `head -c 1000` cut produces **at most one** U+FFFD, and it can only appear at the very end of the sample. Genuine corruption/binary content carries U+FFFD at arbitrary positions. Narrow the check to ignore the tail artifact:

```python
sample = content_sample[:1000]
if "\ufffd" in sample[:-4]:
    return True
```

The existing `non_printable / len > 0.30` fallback (line 898-900) is untouched and still catches binary files (PNG header etc.).

## Verification

- `test_file_operations.py`: **46/46 pass**, including `test_replacement_char_sample_flagged_binary` (latin-1 lossy sample still flagged) and `test_plain_utf8_text_not_flagged`.
- 6 file-tool test files: 159/161 pass. The 2 failures (`test_writes_content`, `test_replace_mode_calls_patch_replace`) are **pre-existing on macOS**: the tests assert `/tmp/out.txt` but the tool normalizes to `/private/tmp/out.txt` (`/tmp` is a symlink on macOS). Confirmed identical on baseline via `git stash`.
- Manual matrix: CJK file → now `is_binary=False`; corrupt file with mid-sample U+FFFD → still `True`; pure ASCII → `False`; real binary PNG → `True`.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.2 (bug is platform-independent; any locale with multibyte text)
- hermes-agent main @ f0c87da61

items.title: [Bug]: Selecting a personality overwrites the manual agent.system_prompt (config clobber, silent data loss)

labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility

items.body:
[test_personality_clobbers_system_prompt.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30857444/test_personality_clobbers_system_prompt.py)

### Bug Description

Selecting a personality **silently overwrites the user's manual `agent.system_prompt`** in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` with the selected personality's prompt text. The manual global prompt (e.g. a short "be concise"-style instruction the user set via `hermes config set agent.system_prompt ...` or `/prompt`) is destroyed with **no backup of the previous value** — silent, unrecoverable data loss of a user config setting.

This is the inverse symptom of #51882: that issue reports the Desktop Settings UI writes *only* `display.personality` (personality silently ignored); this issue reports the TUI Gateway `config.set key=personality` RPC writes *both* fields and thereby clobbers the user's manual `agent.system_prompt`. Both stem from the same root defect — the personality overlay and the durable global manual prompt share the single `agent.system_prompt` field with no separation, and the two write paths (desktop `config.set` RPC vs CLI `/personality`) disagree on whether to write `display.personality` at all, leaving the fields divergent.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set a manual global prompt: `hermes config set agent.system_prompt "manual_prompt_1"` (short, user-authored text).
2. In the desktop app, select any personality (desktop personality picker → routes to `config.set key=personality` RPC), e.g. `personality_1`.
3. Inspect `~/.hermes/config.yaml` — `agent.system_prompt` now contains `personality_1`'s prompt text, not `manual_prompt_1`.
4. Switch to a different personality (`personality_2`) — `agent.system_prompt` now contains `personality_2`'s text.
5. The original `manual_prompt_1` is gone. Nothing on disk records it.

### Expected Behavior

`agent.system_prompt` is a **user-owned, global manual setting** (documented usage: read by `/prompt` at `tui_gateway/server.py:12729` and the CLI ephemeral-prompt path at `cli.py:4508`). Selecting a personality should apply the personality **in-session** via `agent.ephemeral_system_prompt` and record the selection in `display.personality` — it must **not** write into the durable `agent.system_prompt`. The manual prompt must survive personality changes.

### Actual Behavior

The personality branch of the `config.set` RPC (`tui_gateway/server.py:11325-11329`) does:

```python
elif key == "personality":
    pname, new_prompt = _validate_personality(str(value or ""), cfg)
    _write_config_key("display.personality", pname)
    _write_config_key("agent.system_prompt", new_prompt)   # clobbers the manual prompt
```

`_validate_personality` returns the personality's prompt text, which is persisted into `agent.system_prompt`, overwriting whatever the user had set manually. The CLI `/personality` path (`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1353`) has the same defect class but writes only `agent.system_prompt` and never `display.personality` — so the two fields can diverge (observed in the wild: `display.personality` naming one personality while `agent.system_prompt` held a *different* personality's text).

### Affected Component

- Configuration (config.yaml, personality settings)
- Agent Core (system prompt / ephemeral prompt handling)
- Desktop backend (TUI gateway `config.set` RPC)

### Debug Report

Not attached yet — happy to run `hermes debug share` and paste links if needed. Reproduction is deterministic and covered by a unit test (below), so logs are not required to confirm.

### Operating System

CachyOS Linux (Arch-based), kernel 7.1.6-1-cachyos

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) · upstream 3d7dda4c · git install

### Additional Logs / Traceback

Automated reproduction: `tests/tui_gateway/test_personality_clobbers_system_prompt.py` drives the **real** `config.set` handler against a temp `HERMES_HOME` config (real `_write_config_key`/`_save_cfg` disk write; only the live-session pivot is stubbed). Both tests fail on current code via `scripts/run_tests.sh`:

```
FAILED tests/tui_gateway/test_personality_clobbers_system_prompt.py::test_personality_selection_preserves_manual_system_prompt
E   AssertionError: agent.system_prompt was clobbered by the personality selection.
E       expected (manual): 'manual_prompt_1'
E       got (personality): 'personality_1'

FAILED tests/tui_gateway/test_personality_clobbers_system_prompt.py::test_switching_personality_leaves_no_stale_text
E   AssertionError: agent.system_prompt still holds a personality's text after switching personalities; the manual prompt was lost.
E       expected (manual): 'manual_prompt_1'
E       got: 'personality_2'
```

### Root Cause Analysis

`tui_gateway/server.py:11325-11329` (`@method("config.set")` personality branch) — `_write_config_key("agent.system_prompt", new_prompt)` persists the personality's prompt text into the global manual-prompt field. The sibling in-chat `/personality` slash handler (`server.py:12724-12726`) does it *correctly*: it applies the personality only via `agent.ephemeral_system_prompt` and never touches `agent.system_prompt` (its docstring at `server.py:5981` explicitly requires the base system prompt to stay intact to preserve prompt-cache hits). The desktop `config.set` path contradicts that established contract. Introduced by `90890f8f0` ("feat: personality selector"); relocated by the mechanical refactor `f67ca220ab` (no behavior change).

### Proposed Fix

1. `tui_gateway/server.py:11329`: remove `_write_config_key("agent.system_prompt", new_prompt)` — keep `display.personality` + in-session application via `agent.ephemeral_system_prompt` (mirror `_apply_personality_to_session`'s contract).
2. `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1353`: stop writing the personality into `agent.system_prompt`; use a dedicated personality field + in-session ephemeral prompt instead.

Both changes bring the two paths into agreement with #51882's core ask: personality selection must not silently destroy the user's manual `agent.system_prompt`. This is the missing half of the #51882 fix (that PR covers the Desktop Settings UI write path; this covers the `config.set` RPC + CLI paths).

### Related Issues / PRs

- #51882 — Desktop Settings UI writes only `display.personality` (inverse symptom, same root cause)
- #58774 — `/personality` saves to config but doesn't affect current CLI session (`ephemeral_system_prompt` ignored)
- #51155 — Personalities don't change and persist across sessions
- #25964 — personality config persistence (CLI + gateway paths; does not cover `config.set` RPC)

items.title: Bug: ghost '[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]' assistant rows self-replicate (incomplete fix from #73146)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

**Regression from #73146 (incomplete fix): ghost `[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]` assistant rows self-replicate across turns.**

PR #73146 ("keep interrupt-checkpoint scaffolding out of the steered transcript") fixed the *assistant-tail* branch of `_apply_active_turn_redirect` but left the **else branch (tool/user tail)** broken. When a mid-turn steer/correction arrives while the message tail is a tool result or user row, the checkpoint scaffold is still written into the placeholder assistant row:

```python
entry = {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": visible or checkpoint,   # scaffold lands in content when nothing was visible
    "api_content": checkpoint,
}
```

`display_kind="hidden"` only hides the row from **transcript surfaces** (TUI/CLI/desktop projection). The **API replay path** (`conversation_loop.py` `_build_api_messages` / `api_messages` loop) does NOT filter hidden rows — worse, it substitutes `api_content` back into `content` for every user/assistant row. So the provider receives an assistant message whose content is literally:

```
[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]
```

The model reads that as **its own previous reply** and echoes it verbatim. That echoed row is persisted, replayed on the next turn, echoed again — a self-replicating ghost loop. One redirect during a tool turn grew into **61 ghost rows in a single session**; a full `state.db` scan found **281 ghost rows across 44 sessions**, dating back to 2026-07-24.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an agent turn that calls a tool (so the message tail is `assistant(tool_calls) → tool`).
2. While the tool result is pending, send a second message (steer/correction) — e.g. via desktop app Enter-while-busy or gateway `busy_input_mode: interrupt`.
3. `_apply_active_turn_redirect` takes the else branch; the scaffold `[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]` is persisted as an assistant row.
4. Next API call replays that row; the model echoes it; the echoed row is persisted again. Loop repeats.

### Expected Behavior

The interrupted-turn scaffold must never appear in any assistant row's `content` or `api_content`. The model should receive the interrupted context only inside the **user correction's** `api_content` sidecar (exactly as the assistant-tail branch of #73146 already does).

### Actual Behavior

Ghost assistant rows with content `[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]` accumulate in the session DB and keep being replayed/echoed, producing visible fake "interruptions" the user never triggered.

### Proposed Fix

**1. Source (`agent/conversation_loop.py`, `_apply_active_turn_redirect` else branch):** the placeholder assistant row never carries scaffold bytes; the correction carries them in its `api_content`:

```python
placeholder = {"role": "assistant", "content": visible or ""}
if not visible:
    placeholder["display_kind"] = "hidden"
correction = (
    "[Context from the interrupted assistant response]\n"
    f"{checkpoint}\n\n"
    f"{text}"
)
messages.append(placeholder)
messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text, "api_content": correction})
```

**2. Replay guard (same file, API message build loop):** drop legacy ghost rows so pre-fix persisted history cannot keep poisoning new turns:

```python
_ghost_content = msg.get("content")
if (
    msg.get("display_kind") == "hidden"
    and msg.get("role") == "assistant"
    and isinstance(_ghost_content, str)
    and _ghost_content.strip() == "[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]"
):
    continue
```

**3. Data cleanup:** neutralize existing ghost rows in `state.db` (`content=''` + `display_kind='hidden'`) and strip the prefix from any user rows it leaked into.

### Affected Component

Agent core (`agent/conversation_loop.py`) — affects desktop, TUI, and gateway sessions. Related: #71669 (original report, closed by the incomplete #73146).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent main @ b3aa561fa (includes #73146)
- Platform: desktop app

items.title: Webhook/skill-invocation user messages cache as one atomic block — volatile tail bytes invalidate the entire static prefix

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Summary

Webhook-triggered (and likely cron-triggered) skill invocations are sent as a single monolithic **user-role** message: `[IMPORTANT: skill invoked...] + full skill content + volatile event payload`. Anthropic's `cache_control` breakpoint marks this whole block as one atomic unit (`_apply_cache_marker` in `agent/prompt_caching.py`), so even a few bytes of volatile tail content (message ID, timestamp, conversation slug) invalidate the ENTIRE cached block on every invocation — including the ~99.5% of content that is byte-identical across calls.

This is functionally the same problem PR #5713 solved for the **system** prompt (splitting static/session/ephemeral tiers with separate cache_control markers), but that fix never shipped (closed, not merged) and in any case doesn't cover user-role messages, which is where webhook/skill-invocation payloads actually live.

## Evidence (production measurement, not synthetic)

Live account running a webhook route (`helper-events`) invoking a ~21K-char skill on every ticket, ~683 invocations/24h, median inter-ticket gap 80s (well under the 5-min Anthropic cache TTL; 89.7% of gaps ≤5min).

1. Reordered the webhook prompt so static instructions come first and volatile ticket fields (`conversationSlug`, `messageId`, `timestamp`) come last — expecting this alone to fix caching.
2. Fired two live webhook calls 25 seconds apart. Diffed the two resulting rendered user messages: **only the last ~6 of ~1,210 lines differed** (footer with ticket ID/timestamp) — everything else was byte-identical, including the full skill body.
3. Checked actual token usage on both calls via `session_model_usage`:
   - Call 1: `cache_read_tokens=163527`, `cache_write_tokens=85714`
   - Call 2 (25s later, same account, same skill, 99.5%-identical prefix): `cache_read_tokens=163527`, `cache_write_tokens=85714` — **identical, meaning call 2 wrote a full fresh cache instead of reading the shared prefix.**

This confirms the message is being cached/invalidated as one atomic block regardless of how much of it is stable — reordering static content to the front does nothing if there's no *separate* cache_control breakpoint before the volatile tail begins.

## Root cause

`_apply_cache_marker` (agent/prompt_caching.py) and its caller for non-system messages place a single `cache_control` marker at the end of the whole message, rather than splitting a message into `[stable_prefix (own breakpoint), volatile_suffix (uncached)]` the way `_apply_system_cache_markers` does for the system prompt.

## Suggested fix

Generalize the block-splitting approach from PR #5713 (or resurrect/finish it) to also apply to non-system messages that originate from skill/webhook/cron invocation, where the skill body is static per-invocation-route and the event/ticket payload is the only volatile part. Concretely: let skill-invocation message construction emit Anthropic content-block arrays (`[{type: text, text: <skill body>, cache_control: {...}}, {type: text, text: <volatile event data>}]`) instead of a single concatenated string, mirroring the existing system-block splitting logic.

## Impact

Any webhook or cron job that invokes a skill on every trigger with a small amount of per-trigger variable data (timestamps, IDs, payloads) pays full cache-write cost on every single invocation, even when invocations are seconds apart and 99%+ of content is identical. For high-frequency automation this can dominate spend (measured ~58% of total account spend was going to cache writes instead of cache reads on this route alone).

items.title: Desktop UI zoom drops toward 100% after Alt+Tab back (reassert misses 'focus')

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the desktop app's UI zoom drops toward Chromium's 100% baseline when the user Alt+Tabs away from Hermes and back. The saved zoom (e.g. 125%) is **not lost** — `zoom-state.json` still holds 125% — but the visible UI stays shrunk until the user manually re-applies the zoom, because the zoom reassert handler does not listen for the `focus` event that a plain Alt+Tab-back fires.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), desktop app
- Windows 11, display scaling / app UI Scale set to 125%
- Left Alt+Tab (or Alt+Esc) away from the Hermes window and back

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Hermes desktop, set **Settings → Appearance → UI Scale** to 125% (confirmed saved: `%APPDATA%\Hermes\zoom-state.json` contains `"zoomLevel": 1.2239...` ≈ 125%).
2. Alt+Tab to another window/browser, then Alt+Tab back to Hermes.
3. Observe the UI render at a smaller scale (~100% or less) than the saved 125%.

## Expected

The UI should remain at the saved 125%.

## Actual

The UI renders smaller (~Chromium 100% baseline) after returning via Alt+Tab and stays that way until the user re-applies zoom (via Settings → Appearance, or Ctrl+ repeated).

## Root cause (from source analysis)

- `apps/desktop/electron/zoom.ts` — `zoomReassertWindowEvents()` returns `['show', 'restore', 'resized', 'moved']` on non-Linux platforms. **`focus` is not in the list.**
- `installZoomReassertOnWindowEvents()` re-applies the persisted zoom on those events to counteract Chromium dropping webContents zoom on window lifecycle changes (documented in the file's comment: *"Chromium can drop webContents zoom when a BrowserWindow is resized, minimized and restored, or crosses onto a monitor with different display scaling"*).
- On a plain **Alt+Tab-back, Windows fires `focus`** (and `show` in some cases). The zoom-drop occurs, but the reassert handler never fires because it does not listen for `focus`, so the drop is not corrected.
- The persisted value is unaffected — `%APPDATA%\Hermes\zoom-state.json` still holds the user's 125% — confirming this is a live re-render drop, not a settings-loss bug.

## Suggested fix

In `zoomReassertWindowEvents()`, include `'focus'` (and ideally `'activate'`/`'blur'`) for Windows so the persisted zoom is re-applied when the window regains focus via Alt+Tab:

```ts
export function zoomReassertWindowEvents(platform = process.platform) {
  if (platform === 'linux') return ['show', 'restore', 'resize', 'move', 'focus']
  return ['show', 'restore', 'resized', 'moved', 'focus']
}
```

(And/or re-apply the persisted zoom on `webContents` `focus`/`did-start-navigation`.) A debounce may be desirable to avoid churn on repeated focus toggles.

## Workaround

After returning via Alt+Tab, re-select 125% in Settings → Appearance → UI Scale, or press Ctrl+ a couple of times.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop pet does not react to isolated tool failures
items.body:
## Bug Description

The Desktop pet only shows its `failed` state when the entire agent turn emits an `error` event. A tool can fail in isolation and emit `tool.complete` with `payload.error`, while the agent recovers and continues the turn. That failure is visible in the tool result but is not reflected by the pet.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable a Desktop pet with a `failed` animation.
2. Start a turn in the active Desktop session.
3. Let a tool fail without aborting the full turn, such as a terminal command returning a non-zero exit code.
4. Observe the pet when the `tool.complete` event arrives.

## Expected Behavior

The pet briefly shows the `failed` animation for the isolated tool failure, then returns to the steady turn state while the agent continues.

## Actual Behavior

The handler only clears `toolRunning`. The pet never receives an error beat unless the whole turn later fails.

## Environment

- Hermes: current `main` (`9841a6c651`)
- Surface: Desktop
- OS: macOS 26.6
- Python: 3.11.15
- Debug report: N/A; this is a deterministic renderer event-handling gap reproduced and covered by a focused test.

## Root Cause Analysis

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts` already receives `payload.error` on `tool.complete` and uses it to mark the tool part as failed. In the active-session pet branch, however, it only calls `setPetActivity({ toolRunning: false })`. The existing turn-level `error` handler does call `flashPetActivity({ error: true })`.

## Proposed Fix

When an active-session `tool.complete` payload contains `error`, call the existing `flashPetActivity({ error: true })`. Keep the active-session guard so failures in background sessions do not hijack the foreground pet. Add regression coverage for failed, successful, and background-session tool completions.

## PR

I have a focused fix ready and will link it to this issue.

items.title: [Bug]: Agent flush does not adopt live continuation after compression — turns die with misleading "full disk" dialog

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Summary

When LCM/context compression closes a session while a client is still writing against it, the agent turn fails with `session_persistence_failed` and the user is told *"this is often a full disk"*. Disk and `state.db` are healthy. The root cause is a session-identity handoff gap at the flush chokepoint: the store already provides a recovery API (`find_live_compression_child`), the write path just never uses it — it fails closed on the generic path instead of adopting the unique live continuation. Because the new session id is not returned to the client, the stale-id condition reproduces on every follow-up turn until the client reloads.

### Environment (observed)

- Hermes Agent `main` @ `33edfe9a81` (dirty working tree — proposed fix applied locally, not committed)
- Linux 6.1.0-50-amd64 (Debian), Python 3.11.15 (agent venv)
- Hermes WebUI (nesquena/hermes-webui) @ `320789ae` (v1.0.0), browser client, streaming/SSE path
- State DB: `/home/alex/.hermes/state.db`, SQLite `journal_mode=wal`, healthy (416 MB, quick_check ok)
- LCM compression `threshold: 0.35` (default config path)
- Client path: `_run_agent_streaming(session_id=OLD_ID)` against the WebUI server process

### Reproduction (observed 2026-08-07/08, sessions `20260808_184057_f7ad0c`, `9ce135c14445`)

```
LCM leaf compaction finished … / context compression done
Preserved pre-compression session <OLD_ID> … to disk
Session DB append_message failed: Session '<OLD_ID>' is closed by compression;
  adopt its live continuation before appending messages
Turn ended: reason=session_persistence_failed … response_len=0 session=<OLD_ID>
```

Sequence:
1. Compression runs (often 10–45+ s), closes `OLD_ID` (`ended_at` set, `end_reason='compression'`), publishes a unique continuation row.
2. Client sends against `OLD_ID` (`_run_agent_streaming(session_id=…)`).
3. `SessionDB.append_message(s)` raises `CompressionSessionClosedError` (fail-closed by design).
4. `conversation_loop` maps that to `session_persistence_failed` → turn ends without a response, user sees misleading "often a full disk" advice.

Frequency: 9× on 2026-08-08 alone in one agent.log; repeats every turn the client retries the stale id.

**State before the failed append (sanitized):** parent row has `ended_at` set and `end_reason='compression'`; exactly one live child row references it via `parent_session_id`; no other live children.

**Impact / loss semantics:** the turn's messages are not persisted to the closed id and the turn ends with no response (`response_len=0`). Whether the turn content is recoverable depends on client retry after the client-side id refresh; it is not automatically replayed by the agent.

**Workaround:** create/select a new session in the client or hard-reload the WebUI (which re-resolves the session id); not durable for long-running sessions.

**Deterministic reproducer:** not yet provided. The seam can be exercised by a unit test: seed parent+child rows (parent `end_reason='compression'`), call the flush path with the parent id, assert adoption. See Proposed fix for the test list.

### Root cause

- **Store (ok, with one open question):** `hermes_state.py` raises `CompressionSessionClosedError` at the append guard; `find_live_compression_child(parent)` already returns the **unique** live continuation, fail-closed on 0/>1 children. `reopen_orphaned_compression_session` handles the no-child case (shipped via #80487). *Open question:* whether parent close + continuation publish happen in one DB transaction (affects whether "no child" is a true orphan or a short publication window).
- **Agent (gap):** `run_agent.py:_flush_messages_to_session_db_unlocked` catches every `Exception` as a generic write failure and returns `False`; there is no `CompressionSessionClosedError` branch and no adoption.
- **UI (misleading):** generic "often a full disk" text in `run_agent.py` `_format_turn_completion_explanation` regardless of actual cause.
- **Coverage gap:** tests cover the *busy* case (wait-for-lock) and the *orphan* case; nothing covers *closed-with-continuation → adopt*.

**Seam taxonomy (corrected):** compression rotation leaves a closed parent in exactly three states:
1. **Busy** — lock held, append should wait (covered by #75264/#77386).
2. **Closed + unique live child** — append should adopt the child (this issue, unhandled).
3. **Closed + no child** — orphan, recovered at turn start by #80487.

### Proposed fix (part 1 — implemented locally, verified)

In the shared flush chokepoint `_flush_messages_to_session_db_unlocked`:

1. On `CompressionSessionClosedError`, call `find_live_compression_child(self.session_id)` **at most once** (bounded adoption budget = 1 per flush).
2. If a unique live child exists: rebind `self.session_id` to the child and replay only the failed persistence step.
3. If 0 or >1 children (or probe failure): keep failing closed, but set a `_compression_adoption_failed` flag so the turn-completion message names **compression rotation** instead of "full disk".
4. If the adopted child itself is busy/compressed again during replay, the normal Busy/Closed handlers apply (no special casing); a second Closed error fails closed.

**Precision on "atomic":** this is not a systemically atomic operation. `find_live_compression_child` returns a snapshot; between lookup and replay the child may close or re-compress. The safe contract is: adoption is best-effort, bounded (≤1 probe), fail-closed on any uncertainty, and the mutation of `self.session_id` is done while the flush holds the agent's session-write context (single writer per turn). We do **not** claim a shared DB transaction between lookup and append. Batch appends must be idempotent/transactional before replay; this is called out as a required test.

5. `_compression_adoption_failed` must be reset at turn start (it is a per-turn diagnostic flag, not sticky state).

**Part 2 — NOT implemented (separate PR):** returning the adopted session id through the stream (SSE/response) and migrating the WebUI session row so the client targets the continuation directly. Without it, the client stays stale and every follow-up turn re-adopts at flush — functionally OK (persistence stops failing), but the WebUI session index can drift until reload.

### Verification (local, hermes-agent `main`)

**Part 1 — implemented, red before / green after:**
- `tests/run_agent/test_compression_closed_adoption.py` (4: adopt-unique, fail-closed-no-child, fail-closed-ambiguous, exactly-once budget)
- `tests/run_agent/test_compression_race_diagnostics.py` (3: compression message vs disk message)
- Regression: `tests/run_agent/` + `tests/state/` → 1452 passed, 0 failed.
- Live check after agent restart (process started after the patch): stale-id writes adopt the continuation instead of failing; log shows `Adopted live compression continuation <CHILD> for closed session <OLD_ID>`.

**Still needed (test wishlist before a maintainer picks this up):**
- Child closes between lookup and replay (second Closed must fail closed).
- Adopted append hits the Busy wait path.
- Append fails after successful adoption for a real I/O reason (must not be misclassified as compression).
- Flag is reset before the next turn.
- Batch append produces no partial writes/duplicates.
- Two concurrent flushes do not unsafely share/mutate `self.session_id`.
- SSE/response carries the new id (once part 2 lands).
- Integration: stale WebUI id → adoption → response contains child id → next turn writes directly against child.

### Related issues (same seam, orthogonal states)

- #77386 — Busy-wait too short; a longer busy wait does **not** fix the closed-with-child case (that wait only helps while the lock is held).
- #80337 — orphaned parent without continuation; orphan recovery only triggers when no continuation exists, so it is not a competing fix here.
- #80487 — merged orphan-recovery (referenced above).
- #81227 — desktop/tui path with similar misleading copy; listed as adjacent diagnosis, not the same codepath.

### Notes

- `MEDIA_ALLOWED_ROOTS` (media viewer) is unrelated — same "storage" keyword, different subsystem.
- Severity: High/S2. Repeating full turn aborts (`response_len=0`) with a misleading disk diagnosis; no evidence of DB corruption and a manual workaround exist → not Critical/S1. Priority P1 if compression is routinely active in normal WebUI operation, else P2.
- Happy to turn the verified part-1 patch into a PR; part 2 (session-id handoff / WebUI index convergence) is a second logical change (separate PR per project guidelines).

items.title: Anthropic OAuth requests bypass subscription plan limits

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes' native Anthropic OAuth path is classified into Anthropic's extra-usage lane instead of Claude subscription plan limits.

## Reproduction

With valid Claude Code subscription credentials and no Anthropic API key required:

```sh
hermes -z 'Reply with exactly OK.' --provider anthropic -m claude-haiku-4-5 --safe-mode
```

Hermes returns HTTP 400 with `You're out of extra usage`.

The same model, prompt, and credentials through interview-studio's Anthropic adapter return `OK`.

## Expected behavior

Hermes' Anthropic OAuth requests should use Claude subscription plan limits when valid Claude Code credentials are selected.

## Suspected gap

Hermes already sends the OAuth betas, Claude Code user-agent, `x-app`, identity prompt, and OAuth-safe tool names. It does not yet generate the message-dependent Claude Code billing fingerprint used by the working interview-studio adapter.

## Acceptance criteria

- OAuth request kwargs contain a deterministic billing fingerprint derived from the first user message and Claude Code version.
- API-key and third-party Anthropic-compatible requests remain unchanged.
- Behavioral tests cover determinism, message sensitivity, OAuth-only injection, and preservation of prompt-cache markers.
- The real one-shot reproduction succeeds with the configured Claude subscription.

items.title: PR #64172 silently reverted max_iterations default from 500 back to 90 (unrelated to its scope)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

PR #64172 ("refactor(agent): remove the inter-tool delay", merged 2026-07-29) **silently reverted** the default tool-calling iteration limit from `500` back to `90` in the main agent entry points. The PR's body, commit message, comments, and review discussion only cover `tool_delay` removal — nothing mentions `max_iterations`. This looks like an unintentional change brought in by a rebase/cherry-pick from an older branch.

## Evidence

- `1b081e489` (2026-07-26, "feat: raise default tool-calling iteration limit from 90 to 500", teknium1) raised the default to `500` across all entry points: `run_agent.py`, `agent/agent_init.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `cron/scheduler.py`, `tui_gateway/server.py`, `cli.py`, etc.
- `ce9f6712f` (PR #64172) changed it back to `90` in `run_agent.py` and `agent/agent_init.py` — but the PR's stated scope is strictly the inter-tool delay:
  - PR body: only discusses the 1.0s `time.sleep` between sequential tool calls (per-turn tracing, 30-tool turn = 29s asleep).
  - 4 PR comments + the maintainer review: all about `tool_delay` deprecation compatibility (`AIAgent(tool_delay=0)` accepted-but-ignored kwarg, `DeprecationWarning`).
  - Single commit message: "refactor(agent): remove the inter-tool delay" only.
- Current `origin/main` still has `max_iterations: int = 90` at `run_agent.py:446` and `agent/agent_init.py:470` (git blame → `ce9f6712f`), while `tui_gateway/server.py:6537` still uses `_cfg_max_turns(cfg, 500)`.

## Impact

- Inconsistent defaults: the gateway path defaults to `500`, the main agent path (`run_agent.py` / `agent_init.py`) defaults to `90`.
- Sessions that rely on the raised 500-turn limit introduced by #1b081e489 get truncated at 90 tool-calling iterations on the main-agent paths.

## Suggestion

Restore the intended `500` default on the main-agent paths (or confirm the revert was deliberate and document why). Likely a one-line fix per file plus the same in `AGENTS.md`.
